News.title: Hedgehog tragically dies from ‘unnecessary suffering’ after being painted blue and yellow by football yobs
News.content:
VILE ACT Hedgehog tragically dies from ‘unnecessary suffering’ after being painted blue and yellow by football yobs

A HEDGHOG has died after it was painted in the Leeds United football club colours.

Honey, a female hedgehog, went through “unnecessary suffering” prior to her tragic death, when yobs covered her in thick, oil-based blue and yellow paint in Leeds, West Yorkshire.



The poor creature was discovered in garden on July 13 and taken in by rescuers.

Honey was unable to curl into a ball to protect herself deu to her spines “glued” together by the paint.



She also struggled to breathe because of the fumes.

Volunteers at Prickly Pigs Hedgehog Rescue painstakingly scrubbed the paint from each individual spine and gave her pain relief.

But sadly, owner Diane Cook, 51, has now revealed Honey has since died.

She said: “To say that I’m devastated is an understatement and I just cannot believe, or understand, what some people are capable of doing to any living thing.”

Diane added: “We are still working with the local police so can not share any more details about her.”

West Yorkshire Police Wildlife and Rural Crime Team launched an investigation to catch the culprits.



Last weekend, four men aged 44, 21, 17 and 15 were arrested on suspicion of causing unnecessary suffering to a protected animal.

Only the front of her face, stomach and legs had been left untouched, leading rescuers to believe she had been deliberately targeted rather than accidentally brushing against wet paint.

Diane said: “I know from some comments that people have found what happened to her funny or commented that she’s ‘only a hedgehog’, but it does not matter.”

“It is cruel and a completely unnecessary death. When are people going to stop and think about their actions and the impact they are having on nature?”

Diane said the tragedy had left her questioning whether she could continue running the centre.



She said: “It’s times like this when I wonder what is the point of running the rescue. It’s a 24/7 job 365 days a year.”

News.title: Brits in horror bus flip crash with tourists thrown out windows & teen stuck under wreck after ‘high-speed water fight’
News.content:
BUS SMASH TERROR Brits in horror bus flip crash with tourists thrown out windows & teen stuck under wreck after ‘high-speed water fight’

A SIX-MONTH-OLD baby has been rushed to hospital after a safari bus packed with Brit holidaymakers ploughed off-road leaving them bloodied and with broken bones.

About 12 trapped passengers were left “hanging upside down by their seatbelts”, including six children, when their cabrio open-bus careered off road in Alanya, Turkey.



Tragic photos of the wreckage show the Jeep custom-built Safari bus on its side with the metal roof twisted above its 12 seats and its bonnet crumpled.

The shunt also injured a 13-year-old girl who was left trapped underneath the bus while others were sent “flying out their windows.”



Ambulances and Turkish cops were scrambled to the scene of the terrifying crash near Manavgat District, a major tourist attraction with ancient seaside cities and waterfalls.

The vehicle plummeted off a winding road at 3pm local time.



The cabrio bus is thought to have veered off-road at about 40mph when it overtook a partner bus in front during a “water fight” and clattered into branches.

A Brit witness was travelling on the safari tour in an adjoining bus when chaos struck.

He told The Sun: “It was absolutely traumatising. There was lots of blood and broken bones.

“The bus rolled over about three times and landed on its side.



“It just kept rolling off road for about 70 metres.

“There was a kid hanging with his seatbelt around his neck. We had to get him out by climbing from the top of the bus.

“Kids were crying, even kids that weren’t on the bus that crashed were shaking because of how sudden the crash was.



“People immediately rushed out of the other buses to help them.

“When we managed to get people out of the bus their faces were covered in blood and were screaming.”

The dad-of-four had been on an eight-day all-inclusive holiday with his family in Alanya when they witnessed the horror crash.

He added: “It took about 30 minutes for a convoy of ambulances to arrive because we were in the middle of nowhere.

“While we were waiting people were shell-shocked and just laid on the side of the road in agony, in tears.



“One man was sat on the side of the road screaming in pain because his ankle was displaced in the wrong direction.

“The parents of children were crying too. They all escaped death.

“It’s ruined our holiday. We don’t feel safe on these roads. On the replacement bus back to the hotel we were all shaking in fear.”

There were six adult passengers and six children on the bus at the time of the crash – most of whom were British tourists.

They had been on a safari tour run by Alanya-based holiday firm Tony Montana excursions – named after the playboy mafia superboss.



Families were on an open bus safari excursion in a convoy of seven from Türkler, Alanya, through the Taurus Mountains in South Turkey.

It promises to take tourists on an “action-packed” and “entertainment-heavy” tour across remote viewpoints that includes a “water battle” mid journey while driving.

The road trip lasts about eight hours and is priced at about £20-a-head.

It also includes a 1-hour boat cruise on Green Lake near the coast, a traditional Turkish lunch by the water, and stops at the Manavgat Waterfall and ancient Seleucia.

A Tony Montana Excursions spokesperson said: “Tony Montana Excursions acts as a booking agent for tours around the Antalya Region. We do not directly have involvement in the day’s activities.

“Ourselves, along with the majority of local tour operator, s provide a platform connecting tourists to facilitating businesses.

“First and foremost our primary concerns are the welfare of all participants. We have as of yet not spoken to all parties and feel it inappropriate to make comment at this time.”

News.title: Teacher accused of having sex with boy, 10, she strapped to bed was ‘found under covers with him by his sister’
News.content:
'PAEDO' MISS Teacher accused of having sex with boy, 10, she strapped to bed was ‘found under covers with him by his sister’

A TEACHER accused of having sex with a ten-year-old boy was found under the covers with him by his sister, a court heard.

Deborah Franklin, 65, allegedly blindfolded and strapped the pupil to her bed so she could sexually tickle him with a feather over a four-year period.



The married prep school teacher met the alleged victim, now in his 40s, when he was nine and joined her class.

Franklin – then aged around 30 – later became his private tutor and allegedly went on to have “countless” sexual encounters with him.



She is accused of eight counts of gross indecency with a boy under 14 between 1991 and 1995 at a preparatory school in Hertfordshire.

St Albans Crown Court heard from the boy’s sister, who said the teacher spent a lot of time at their home.

She told jurors that on one occasion, she found Franklin “under the covers reading a book to [the complainant]”.

The sister, who can’t be named, described Franklin as “fun” and “charismatic”.

She added: “I thought she was cool, I liked her. She was very likeable.

“She was in the house often. She became a family friend. She came on Saturday afternoons. I saw her quite a lot.”



The sibling said her brother reported Franklin to the police after finding out she was still working at the same school in 2024.

He told the court how he was in the garage of his home when Franklin asked him: “Do you want to touch me?”

The boy continued: “She kissed me on the lips and we started to touch.”

He also claimed Franklin referred to herself as his girlfriend and warned him they had to be “cautious”.

Describing another alleged encounter, the complainant said: “She asked me to come on the bed. I think it was her marital bed.



“I remember her tying me. Tying my arms down… She had a feather. Some kind of feathery gloves and fur. She tickled me. I remember being strapped down to the bed and blindfolded.

“She was surprised I didn’t enjoy it. Being bound to the bed it disturbed me in my teenage life when I began to understand what it would have been for her.

“At the time, I don’t think I was terrified. I wasn’t. I don’t remember being scared. But it began to bother me when I was around 14… I was tied to the posts, blindfolded and she was tickling me naked and I remember her being surprised I didn’t enjoy it. Her kind of quizzing me why I didn’t enjoy it, what I didn’t like.

“I was there for some hours. I remember us coming back to it later and having sex on her bed.”

A former school friend told jurors Franklin and the boy had a “very close” and “flirtatious” relationship and would hold hands on school trips.



Another friend said the pair would sit “very close” to each other when watching television.

They said: “He would sit very much in Mrs Franklin’s arms, as you would see a boyfriend and a girlfriend sitting together, and at moments tickling his arm.

“There was a lot of laughing, talking, whispering. I felt very much outside of it. I felt left out, that was my best friend.”

The court was told Franklin branded the allegations as a “lot of rubbish” following her arrest.

She denies eight counts of gross indecency with a boy under 14.



The trial continues.

News.title: We live underneath the M4 – it is Britain’s ‘biggest gazebo’ and we get a surprise benefit during the summer
News.content:
TUCKED under one of the UK’s busiest motorways lives a group of residents who confess to loving life thanks to the surprising benefits of being so close to the highway.

Port Talbot in Wales is home to hundreds of families who enjoy living under the M4 despite roughly 130,000 vehicles thundering over it everyday.



The town, famed for its smoggy steelworks and legendary actors Richard Burton, Anthony Hopkins and Michael Sheen, is also known for the busy motorway.

The M4 is a 189- mile route that runs from London to Carmarthenshire in West Wales.



Neighbours love their highway to heaven – using the concrete girders as a pole for their washing lines and others praising its perfect shelter from sun or rain.

Clare Reeves, a Tesco checkout worker, moved next door to the motorway just two years ago and is already mortgage free.



She moved 70 miles from Bristol to buy the family home for £136,000.

Clare, 49, said: “We bought the house obviously knowing that the motorway was here. If we had thought it would be a problem we wouldn’t have bought it.

“My husband sometimes sleeps with earplugs in but I have got used to the noise.”

Opposite Clare lives Evie Cursons, a 20-year-old mental health support worker.



She lives on Pont Street, one of several roads of terraced houses which became cul-de-sacs when the M4 was built at one end of it.

Evie said: “It is like a safety net. I’ve been here all my life and it just feels like it adds a real sense of community.

“I have never known any different but when I was a child we could always play in the street and our parents wouldn’t have to worry about where we were.



“I’m pretty sure all the houses have double glazing and so you can’t hear the road at all when they are shut but when it’s been hot obviously you can hear it but you get used to it pretty quickly – it’s like white noise.”

Grandmother Jean Heatman, 73, is grateful for the motorway which looms directly over her back garden on Ynys Street.

“I have lived here for 53 years and it has never bothered me,” she said.



“As the years have gone by the traffic has been a bit more busy but it is not a problem.”

The retired kitchen assistant said the road above has provided a valuable shelter over the years.

“During covid when people were not allowed to meet indoors so children’s dance groups would gather under the bridge to hold their classes and it was lovely to see.

“And at the moment with it being so hot I can take my dog for a walk up and down here and stay in the shade to keep it cool.”

Another neighbour dubbed the bridge her “free gazebo” while another man said it meant “we could buy the house so cheap.”



Around the corner is Llewellyn Street – where 150 homes on one side of the road were demolished to make way for the M4.

Pensioner Jean Davies, 85, moved onto the road in 1963, and witnessed the houses opposite her own being replaced by the motorway.

The mother-of-two said: “It was built while we were living here so we have seen lots of changes over the years.



“We were never worried about the noise from the road, you soon get used to it, and we have the main trainline running behind the garden too.

“It used to be a lovely street where everyone knew who the neighbours were. Now people are coming and going all the time.”

Widow Jean also bemoaned the council for failing to look after the motorway underpass – which has been allowed to grow wild as part of a conservation effort.



“They used to cut the grass,” she said. “Now it is just such a mess.”

College student Leilea Jammali, 18, said she feared “horror stories” when her family moved across Port Talbot to King Street in the shadow of the M4 in 2021.

She said: “My friends would say about the pollution, the noise, or that the house was going to be shaking from all the traffic but honestly it has been fine.



“The only time you notice it would be if a really big lorry was overhead and blocked out the sun. It could be like a total eclipse.

“We love living here.”

Kirsty Bowd, 36, says she loves living on King Street with the M4 rattling above just a stone’s throw away.
