“I have been here 14 years and my friends are all living here. We don’t even notice the road really.

“All the neighbours here support each other and I absolutely love it.”

News.title: Boy, 16, charged with double murder of girl, 15, & brother, 9, in horrific home shooting as cops warn of dating violence
News.content:
A TEEN boy has been charged with the murders of a 15-year-old girl and her nine-year-old brother after they were found shot dead inside their family home.

The 16-year-old suspect was arrested just one day after the siblings were laid to rest.



Keith Maurice James Jr. has been charged as an adult with two counts of first-degree murder over the deaths of Giovanna “Gigi” Myrie and her younger brother Steve Allen in Gwynn Oak, Maryland.

The siblings were allegedly gunned down inside their home on Talles Road on July 7 before their parents returned home and made the horrifying discovery, according to CBS.



Police said James knew both children and had some form of personal relationship with Giovanna, although detectives have not confirmed whether it was a friendship or romantic relationship, Fox Baltimore reported.

Baltimore County Police Chief Robert McCullough said investigators believe the suspect had visited the home before the killings.

“All I can say is we do know that he had been at the home before, maybe even several days prior, that we can confirm at least on, to our knowledge, on July 4th,” McCullough said.

Detectives also allegedly placed James in the neighborhood on the night of the shootings using surveillance footage.



“He was on camera in several ways throughout the community. He had been in the area prior to the crime and, of course, he was in the area after the crime,” the chief said.

James is being held without bail at the Baltimore County Detention Center.

Police have not revealed a possible motive and said they are still trying to determine how the 16-year-old allegedly obtained the gun.

McCullough described the case as deeply disturbing, saying: “It’s troubling when you consider how horrific this crime was carried out. It was terrible.

“When you reflect on the fact that the child just turned 16, he carried on this crime, and did it in the manner that he did, it’s troubling.”



The police chief also said the investigation pointed to a wider issue affecting young people.

“We need to make sure we know who our kids are associating with. The final issue is dating violence, teen violence between people who have relationships. We need to be mindful of those things,” said McCullough.

He added investigators took extra care because of the suspect’s age.



“It took longer than I wanted it to; however, we had to make sure that we put together a very airtight case considering the age of the suspect in this case,” he said.

The arrest came a day after mourners gathered at St. Casimir Church for the siblings’ funeral.

Family and friends were black and yellow in tribute to the children’s favorite colors before the pair were taken to their final resting place.

In a statement shared through the family, their loved ones said: “Steve and Gigi were deeply loved by so many, and their love, laughter, and beautiful spirits will forever remain in our hearts.”

They also thanked supporters, adding: “Your kindness has brought us comfort beyond words.”



Baltimore County Executive Kathy Klaumeier praised detectives after the arrest.

“I would like to say how sad a day like today is,” she said.

“Please keep the families in your prayers. I am pleased that the police department did such a great, quick job on this part of the situation.”

Baltimore City Councilmember Julian Jones said he was shocked by the allegations.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I am just taken back by the fact that young people, at the age of 16 years old, would not only have access to a gun but have the propensity to actually murder someone, murder two people,” he said.



“We can’t stop random acts of violence, but just trust and believe that when these violence are perpetrated here in Baltimore County, we will not leave any stones unturned before we make an arrest and take that person to justice.”

News.title: Moment cops about to smash into house in drugs raid are told through Ring doorbell ‘just come in, the door’s open’
News.content:
THIS is the moment cops about to smash down a door and raid a home are told through a Ring doorbell to “come in.”

Armed officers were preparing to carry out a drugs raid on the home in Melksham, Wiltshire, on Tuesday when they were politely welcomed in.



Video footage of the bizarre bust was shared online after it was captured by a spectator.

A team of cops armed with crowbars and power tools can be seen rushing towards the front door of the property.



Several officers flank either side of the doorway before one proceeds to lift a red battering ram.

As he prepares to smash down the door, his colleagues line up by the garden fence.



Some officers can be seen peeking into the windows of the home as they get ready to storm the building.

Before the cops get a chance to smash their way into the house, however, the occupier can be heard saying “just come in, the door is open.”

Confused, the officer with the tools hands the battering ram to a colleague who puts it on the floor.

Another cop then steps up and checks if the door is unlocked as his colleagues clamber over the garden fence.

Officers appear to be attempting to surround the property before they enter.



Pushing the handle down and realising the property is open, one of the armed cops looks up at his colleagues and nods his head.

He then swings the door wide and the group charge through the entrance.

Inside the home, a 19-year-old man was taken into custody by the team of officers.

He was arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of controlled drugs.

Wiltshire Police said he remains in custody at this time.



Officers also seized a cache of Class A and B drugs from the home during their unchallenged raid.

Cops also recovered two swords and a suspected county lines drug phone from the house.

The Sun has contacted Wiltshire Police for comment.

News.title: Trump bombs Iran from UK airbase for first time after Burnham allows ‘defensive strikes’ in reversal of Starmer decision
News.content:
DONALD Trump has used a UK airbase to launch strikes on Iran for the first time under Andy Burnham’s new leadership.

The US deployed a B-1 bomber from RAF Fairford after the new Prime Minister allowed for “defensive strikes“ on Tehran.



The long-range plane, which can carry 24 2,000lb bombs and travels at the speed of sound, was used to hit Iranian military targets, sources told Axios.

Burnham agreed to continue the UK’s policy of allowing the US to use the air base in Gloucestershire this week for purely “defensive strikes”, according to Bloomberg.



There had been some back and forth between ousted PM Sir Keir Starmer and Trump at the start of the war.

Starmer had ruled out Washington using its bases for weeks despite intense pressure from Trump and his top allies.



The PM eventually folded and allowed the US to use RAF bases like Fairford and Diego Garcia for defensive strikes.

In his final hours in Downing Street, Starmer chaired a COBRA meeting on UK policy to address the renewed US bombardment of Iran.

Ministers chose to continue to allow the bases to be used and Burnham quickly agreed – despite the risk of angering anti-war Labour voters.

It comes as the war in the Middle East continues to ramp up with the US on its 12th consecutive night of strikes on Tehran.



Trump has vowed to obliterate Iranian bridges and power plants for every ship Tehran shoots at in the Strait of Hormuz.

Burnham’s newly appointed Foreign Secretary, Ed Miliband, has today told foreign ministers that the UK would “work intensively with others to seek to de-escalate” the Iran conflict.

Miliband also said he welcomed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed in June between the US and Iran.



This is despite the very first point of the MoU being an “immediate and permanent termination of military operations on all fronts”.

Relentless attacks from both Iran and the US have rained down across the Middle East for almost two weeks now – breaching the MoU entirely.

An enraged Trump has vowed to destroy the Islamic Republic after each side accused the other of breaking the ceasefire terms.

The US president wrote on Truth Social overnight: “Any time Iran shoots at a ship in the Strait of Hormuz, whether it be by Missile, Rocket, Drone, or any other weapon, the United States will bomb and destroy ONE BRIDGE OR POWER PLANT.”

Shortly after, Iran targeted US assets in Kuwait, Jordan and Bahrain.



The Iranian Revolutionary Guard (IRGC) also said the Strait of Hormuz was “completely closed” as it continues to wage war in the waterway.

The IRGC said it stopped three oil tankers from passing through the strait.

One tanker was set ablaze and two others turned back after trying to pass through a mined section of the strait, according to Iranian state media.



About 15 per cent of global maritime trade passes through the Red Sea – a passage enclosed by two narrow waterways – Bab al-Mandeb and the Suez Canal.

Iranian proxy terror group the Houthis have also now re-entered the conflict after claiming to have attacked two oil tankers in the Red Sea.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They said the Encelia and Layla vessels had been blitzed, with both vessels belonging to Saudi Arabia.

The Houthis said they targeted the ships with drones and cruise missiles for allegedly violating this blockade.

News.title: Russian fighter jet crashes & explodes near Moscow ‘in feared friendly fire shootdown of Putin’s prized £37m warplane’
News.content:
A RUSSIAN fighter jet has crashed and gone up in flames after a suspected friendly fire shootdown near Moscow.

Vladimir Putin‘s prized £37million warplane was engulfed in a huge fireball after its pilot desperately steered it away from civilians.



The military aircraft came down and exploded in the village of Lutsino during “a training flight”.

Local reports have speculated it could have mistakenly been shot down by Russian air defences amid paranoia over repeated Ukrainian drone strikes.



Kyiv has been launching salvos of UAVs aimed at Putin’s energy and trade infrastructure in a bid to disrupt civilian life and push the tyrant towards the negotiating table.

It is still unclear what caused the fighter jet crash and authorities are yet to confirm its circumstances.

The aircraft has been identified in Russian Telegram channels as a Sukhoi Su-57, which cost around £37million each.

They are the Kremlin’s most modern operational fighter and Moscow’s answer to America’s F-22 Raptor and F-35 Lightning II.



The pilot reportedly remained at the controls long enough to direct the stricken jet away from nearby homes.

He is believed to have ejected at the last possible moment.

Eyewitnesses described seeing the jet crash and a parachute descending nearby.

One image showed what appeared to be a parachute hovering above the site of the crash with a person seen dangling underneath.

A local said: “The plane came down, and a parachute was descending nearby.



“It practically happened right before our eyes. He definitely ejected, but I do not know whether he survived.”

Another witness said: “The pilot ejected, and then the fighter jet exploded.”

Black smoke was seen rising in a column from the crash site.

Pro-Kremlin Telegram channel Mash claimed the pilot survived, while Baza reported that he had managed to eject “in time”.

Russian authorities have opened a criminal case on “violations of flight rules or preparation for them” in the wake of the crash.



Staunch pro-war Russian Telegram channel Romanov Light said: “A great many questions should be asked of the local air-defence forces.”

The crash site is close to Kubinka military airbase, west of Moscow, although it has not been established that the fighter took off from there.

The twin-engined Su-57 is Russia’s first purported stealth fighter and is designed for both air-superiority and ground-attack missions.

Russia has used Su-57s during the war against Ukraine, generally launching long-range weapons from safe airspace rather than risking the scarce jets close to Ukrainian defences.

It comes amid a series of successful Ukrainian strikes on the battlefield and beyond the frontline.



Kyiv has launched several barrages of drones on “Russia’s Amazon” in recent weeks – sparking massive infernos ripping through the retail giant’s warehouses.

On Wednesday, key logistics hubs run by e-commerce firm Wildberries were set ablaze leaving over £1billion in damages.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The assault was part of Ukraine’s endgame blitz – a series of deep strikes targeting energy and logistics hubs in Russia.

News.title: Europe weather chaos as Spain faces 49C heatwave and 'firenado' seen in France
News.content:
Europe weather chaos as Spain faces 49C heatwave and 'firenado' seen in France

Spain is in the midst of its third heatwave, with temperatures forecast to hit 44C on Thursday and potentially climb to 49C on Sunday, while evacuations have been ordered in France

View 8 Images Anomaly maps show temperatures surging well above average in southern Europe next week (Image: WXCharts)

Europe is being gripped by hot weather as temperatures in Spain could soon climb to 49C, while France faces evacuations and a 'firenado' amid raging wildfires.

‌



The soaring temperatures have fuelled wildfires across Spain, France and Italy, with a 'fire tornado' - caused by fierce winds carrying flames - tearing through woodland near Saumos, close to Lacanau in the Gironde department of south-west France. The wildfire there burned more than 2,000 hectares and forced the evacuation of more than 10,000 people overnight into Thursday.

‌



Meanwhile, Spain's national weather agency, AEMET, warned that the latest heatwave, which began on Tuesday, is expected to last all week and said temperatures could hit 44C on Thursday.

‌



View 8 Images The 'firenado' spotted in France (Image: x)

UK weather maps show 39C heatwave and hottest day of year as 10 counties hit 38C READ MORE :

Are you worried about the extreme summer weather? Take our poll and have your say READ MORE :

The GFS weather model suggests areas in and around Seville could see temperatures as high as 49C on August 2. If so, Spain would surpass its highest recorded temperature of 47.6C, set in La Rambla, Córdoba province, in August 2021.

AEMET warned on Wednesday that the risk of wildfires was "very high or extreme" across most of mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands.

‌



View 8 Images Maximum temperatures at 6pm on July 30 (Image: WXCharts)

Firefighters in central Spain battled a blaze on Wednesday that has burned more than 32,000 hectares in one of the country's largest wildfires on record. The fire, which broke out on July 16 near La Mierla in Guadalajara province, north-east of Madrid, forced the evacuation of several hundred people.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez visited the area on Wednesday and called for a pact between political parties to fight climate change. "Year after year we clearly see how climate change kills and destroys wealth in our communities," he said in the village of Tamajón. "This isn’t politics. It is science, it’s about facts."

‌



View 8 Images Firefighters tried to extinguish fires burning trees using a wildland water truck near Le Porge, south-west France, on July 23 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

In Italy, wildfires continued to burn on Wednesday in several parts of the Casaboli forest, located in the Sicilian mountains between the towns of Monreale and Pioppo.

In France, the Gironde prefecture said around 500 firefighters had been deployed to tackle the blaze as "the situation remains unfavourable".

‌



View 8 Images Spain could see record-breaking highs of 49C on August 2 (Image: WXCharts)

More than 10,000 people were evacuated as a precaution, including tourists staying at eight holiday camps and campsites in the region. More than 1,000 residents living along the forest edge were also evacuated.

Nine municipalities opened reception and respite centres for evacuees, where more than 2,500 people took shelter, the prefecture said.

‌



Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said more than 12,500 wildfires have broken out in France since the start of the year, burning almost 44,000 hectares.

View 8 Images The aftermath of a wildfire that ravaged the area near the town of Albendiego, in the Guadalajara province, north-east of Madrid, pictured on July 22 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Scientists have warned that human-driven climate change is increasing the frequency and intensity of heatwaves and drought, creating conditions that make wildfires more likely and more destructive.

‌



It comes after a Met Office report published in May found that there is an 86 per cent chance that at least one year between 2026 and 2030 will be hotter than 2024, currently the planet's warmest year on record.

View 8 Images Wildfires continued to burn in several parts of Sicily, Italy on July 22 (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

It also found that there is a 91 per cent chance that global temperatures will temporarily exceed 1.5C above pre-industrial levels in at least one of the next five years.

Article continues below

If global warming exceeds 1.5C - the target limit set by the Paris Agreement - the risk of severe climate impacts rises sharply.

View 8 Images A firefighting helicopter works to extinguish a blaze that broke out late on July 21 at El Cerro del Andevalo in Huelva, south-west Spain (Image: DAVID ARJONA/EPA/Shutterstock)

These include ecosystem damage, species extinction, more extreme weather, food and water insecurity, heat-related deaths and the loss of ancient ice sheets in Greenland and Antarctica, which would cause sea levels to rise dramatically.

News.title: British Gas boss warns 'time is running short' to protect winter supply
News.content:
British Gas boss warns 'time is running short' to protect winter supply

The head of energy giant Centrica is urging the new government to back investment in the UK's largest gas storage site

View 2 Images British Gas boss Chris O’Shea (Image: PA Archive/PA Images)

The UK faces a race against time to ensure it has enough gas stored for winter, a top boss has warned.

‌



Chris O’Shea, head of British Gas owner Centrica, warned “time is running short” to ensure the country’s largest gas storage site remains open. He said the vast undersea facility, called Rough, would be “close to exhausted” by the winter, as the firm called on the government to step in.

‌



The former gas field beneath the North Sea could store enough gas for up to 30 days but needs to be upgraded. Centrica says it is costing it £10million a month to keep it open.

‌



It comes as growing concerns about gas supplies has sent wholesale energy prices soaring again. The wholesale price of gas in Europe has jumped 50% in the past month as countries battle for supplies against competition from the Far East due to the ongoing impact of the Middle East war.

Christoph Halser, a gas analyst at energy consultancy Rystad, told the FT: “Back in March and April we had just come out of winter and demand was pretty low. Now we are running out of time a bit as this year’s winter approaches, so the price is reacting.”

View 2 Images UK has significantly less gas storage than countries in Europe (Image: Getty)

‌



Mr O’Shea, who has spoken to new energy secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh, revealed Centrica has not put any gas into its Rough facility this summer and, by this winter, it will “be close to exhausted, producing less than 2% of what it could deliver if redeveloped.

“Rough could strengthen the UK’s energy security and reduce exposure to volatile international gas markets,” but he warned “time is running short.”

Centrica is lobbying the government to back a £2billion project to revive Rough as an enlarged storage site, Mr O’Shea calling it an “important strategic asset.” Centrica would stump up the money but says it needs guarantees when it comes to a return on its investment for decades to come.

‌



Mr O'Shea revealed the company was talking to government about a short-term deal boost its storage for this winter in a move, he said, could help keep bills down.

“We are willing to do something short-term for this coming winter,” Mr O’Shea said. “But every day we lose is a day’s less gas we can get in there. They probably don’t want to go into this winter with less than four days of peak demand in storage capacity.”

Free plug-in batteries could be handed out to families to cut energy bills READ MORE :

Wholesale gas prices in the UK have also risen sharply again in recent weeks as the heatwaves have seen a rise in demand for air conditioning, especially in London.

‌



The sweltering temperatures have also reduced output from parts of France’s nuclear power plant fleet, forcing them to rely on gas-fired power stations, further increasing demand for gas.

The UK and Europe also rely on liquefied natural gas (LNG), which arrives in supertankers, to help meet demand. However, several shipments have diverted to Asia as buyers are willing to pay a higher price.

Mr O’Shea’s comments came as Centrica revealed the company had shed 1,300 jobs in recent months, including 500 cuts announced last month as part of efforts to overhaul its customer services and support teams.

‌



Centrica said some of the cuts involve natural attrition, whereby a person’s job is not replaced when they choose to leave or retire.

The overhaul is a response to structural changes in customer behaviour, with average customer calls falling by 20% year-on-year, and around 90% now using digital methods of support, according to Centrica.

Chief executive Chris O’Shea said: “We’re creating an awful lot of jobs, we are growing, but we’ve got to reflect the changes in customer behaviour and we’ve got to give customers what they want.

‌



“It’s a sensitive time when people are leaving your organisation but we’re working with our trade unions and we’re working with our colleagues in order to do this in the best way possible.”

Mr O’Shea said he welcomed Andy Burnham’s decision to cut VAT from energy bills from October 1, which is set to save the typical household £45 a year. But he added: “Would I rather we had more targeted support? I would, and I suspect the Prime Minister would rather more targeted support as well.

“But that will take some time. So I think we should applaud the move to remove VAT from energy bills, but we should also give them a bit of time.”

Article continues below

Centrica announced a profit of £497million for the six months to June 30, compared with £549million the same time a year ago.

News.title: Teens forced to stop people recording West Mersea beach tragedy as girl and woman died
News.content:
Teens forced to stop people recording West Mersea beach tragedy as girl and woman died

People who tried to rescue a family after they got into difficulty at West Mersea beach in Essex were forced to stop others from recording the incident, it has been claimed

View 4 Images A mother and her teenage daughter died after getting into difficulty in the water off the coast of West Mersea (Image: Humphrey Nemar/Daily Mirror)

People who tried to rescue a family after they got into difficulty at an Essex beach had to stop others from recording the incident, it has been claimed.

‌



A woman in her 40s and a teenage girl sadly died following the incident near Seaview Avenue, West Mersea, on Wednesday evening.

‌



Essex Police said officers were called by the ambulance service at 5.35pm on Wednesday after reports that several people had got into difficulty in the water.

‌



A third person remains in hospital in a serious condition, while two others are in hospital with non-life-threatening injuries, police said. Those involved are understood to be family members.

View 4 Images A third person - believed to be a seven-year-old boy - remains in hospital in a serious condition (Image: © 2026 PA Media, All Rights Reserved)

West Mersea beach tragedy as woman and girl die despite heroic actions of local teens READ MORE :

Girl and woman in 40s die at Mersea Island beach as hero teens race to save family READ MORE :

Three teenagers who work at the Seaview Beach Diner were among the first on the scene after hearing a commotion outside and raced to try to save those in the water.

‌



One of the teenagers, Leonie Powling, 19, told the Mirror: "We had someone run to the cafe saying they needed help, so we all stopped what we were doing and ran to the beach.

"We saw some people on the beach, and there were still some casualties in the water. We started running around, trying to find anyone with a kayak or a paddleboard. We couldn't just run into the water because there was a riptide, and everyone would've just been sucked in.

View 4 Images Emergency services at West Mersea beach on Wednesday evening (Image: Daniel Rees/Newsquest/SWNS)

‌



"We were sat with a casualty making sure she was okay. There was another casualty we got out of the water, who was struggling to breathe at that point. One of the workers went up to her, patted her on the back and said: 'You need to make yourself throw up.'

"We got some people out, safe and okay. One is in serious condition, but will hopefully get better. With the other two, we're just thinking about the family. It's heartbreaking."

Leonie's father Carl Powling, 55, Colchester City councillor for Mersea & Pyefleet Ward, said the teen heroes were forced to stop people recording the horrific incident on their phones.

‌



View 4 Images The teenage girls were 'stopping people trying to film' the emergency response (Image: BBC)

He said: "The actions of the girls are actually really admirable. From the onset of the incident, where the members of public called the ambulance, emergency services, the people that went in to help try and pull people out - the fact that the three girls went out to assist.

"One of them was on the phone directing the police exactly where to come, you know, directions down to Mersea. Then the way they tried to move people back, the crowds back, the level-headedness and calmness of them is actually, for their age group, phenomenal. They saw everything that was going on.

Article continues below

"They were stopping people trying to film it, keep people away. Then the RNLI, the coastguard, everyone arrived, emergency services and them. But what they did, it's admirable for the local teenagers here, to be fair."

News.title: Sightseeing helicopter crashes and lands on two tourists in terrifying footage
News.content:
Sightseeing helicopter crashes and lands on two tourists in terrifying footage

A sightseeing helicopter plunged to the ground and struck two tourists who suffered head injuries, one more seriously, in Qinghai Province, China

Moment sightseeing helicopter plunges to ground injuring tourists

Two tourists were rushed to hospital after they were hit by a helicopter which crash-landed in China.

‌



The sightseeing helicopter plunged to the ground and struck the spectators who suffered head injuries, one more seriously, in the incident in Qinghai Province on Tuesday.

‌



In the footage, the yellow gyroplane was seen performing a low-altitude demonstration flight as part of a three-aircraft formation.

‌



But it suddenly span wildly out of control as smoke could be seen coming from the back of it. The helicopter plummeted to the ground, veering to its left and landing on two people watching on who could do nothing as the aircraft struck them.

View 3 Images Plumes of smoke coming from the back of the helicopter (Image: JamPress)

British Airways flight makes emergency landing after fault discovered mid-air READ MORE :

The crash happened at Chaka Sky No. 1 Scenic Area beside the salt lake in Qinghai Province. The tourists remained conscious on arrival at Ulan County People’s Hospital before transfer to a larger facility in Haixi Prefecture.

‌



Officials from the Ulan County Joint Investigation Group said: “A self-rotating rotorcraft crash-landed, injuring two people on the ground. The victims were sent for medical treatment at the first opportunity. Their vital signs are currently stable.”

View 3 Images The helicopter crashed to the ground in China (Image: JamPress)

The group added that the aircraft has been seized and the scenic spot was closed while the cause is probed. Early indications suggest wake turbulence from a nearby gyroplane may have triggered the loss of control.

‌



The occupants of the Harbin XLI gyroplane, which can carry two or three people, escaped injury. The investigation is ongoing.

Meanwhile, an aviation influencer died in China in front of more than 1,000 fans after his ultralight aircraft plunged from the sky and burst into flames during a livestream last September.

Tang Feiji was broadcasting live when his twin-rotor craft took a steep turn and nosedived into Jiange County, central China. Viewers were horrified and flooded the stream's chat with messages pleading for someone to "call the emergency services" and "save him"

Article continues below

View 3 Images Two people were hit by the helicopter (Image: JamPress)

Despite their desperate pleas, it was too late, and Tang, 55, was pronounced dead at the scene from the impact. Tang was well-known on the internet in Guangyuan City, Sichuan Province for his frequent flying content, with over who had around 100,000 followers on the Chinese social media platform Douyin.

Just moments before the fatal crash, he had briefly landed to simply adjust his camera before another quick takeoff. While flying the plane, the influencer was not wearing any form of helmet or parachute for safety.

News.title: Aldi's £15 'fast drying' laundry gadget like £40 B&Q version coming out Thursday
News.content:
Aldi's £15 'fast drying' laundry gadget like £40 B&Q version coming out Thursday

Shoppers can spend less at Aldi with its new Special Buy deal coming out in a few days

View 3 Images Aldi is selling a similar version for less and it's coming out on Thursday (Image: Aldi)

Aldi is updating its range of Middle Aisle Special Buys over the coming week, with more cleaning gadgets on the way, designed to help shoppers at home. The budget supermarket is popular with customers across the country for regularly offering a variety of homeware essentials at affordable prices.

‌



A fresh collection of items is due to land in stores next Thursday, July 30. Several of these will be laundry and cleaning tools, with one item similar to a pricier version on sale at B&Q.

‌



In a few days, Aldi will release its new Addis Three-Tier Airer for £14.99. It comes in either black or grey and is said to offer "a straightforward way to dry more clothes".

‌



The airier may be handy for shoppers who wish to cut down on their tumble dryer energy usage and electricity costs by taking advantage of the warm summer weather to dry clothes outside in a 'speedy' way. The airer offers 16 meters worth of drying space.

It has pull-out arms to create extra hanging drying space and comes with a built-in anti-collapse mechanism that folds down "easily" for sleek storage. It can also be locked in place using the "specially designed locking clip".

View 3 Images Aldi's Addis Three-Tier Airer for £14.99 (Image: Aldi)

‌



Aldi says that the "drying bars have been spaced to maximise the airflow to speed up drying time". The supermarket also says it comes with a three-year warranty and that its design is "strong, yet lightweight".

B&Q is selling a similar airer online, which, although it looks similar at a glance, costs more. The DIY retailer is offering an Indoor and Outdoor Clothes Airer for £39.99.

B&Q says the £40 airer is "easy to use" and "provides a reliable solution for drying clothes efficiently and maintaining a tidy home environment". The store's version is also made of powder-coated steel that is "rust-proof and waterproof".

‌



View 3 Images B&Q's Indoor and Outdoor Clothes Airer for £39.99 (Image: B&Q)

There are three hanging levels with a drying capacity of 20 meters. B&Q says it is designed to make it easier to organise laundry and takes up much less space than vertical models. It adds: "A compact drying solution for indoor and outdoor use... Save energy and money by using this extra-large airer to dry laundry naturally and the energy costs that come from tumble drying."

Another cleaning and laundry gadget coming to Aldi stories on Thursday is the £2.49 Peg Basket and Sock Hanger. Aldi says the contraption helps "keep small garments organised and secure while drying".

Article continues below

The affordable item features a foldable design, with adjustable hooks and includes 36 pegs. The store says: "Lightweight and convenient for everyday laundry use. Choose from Sock Hanger or Peg Basket in Grey or Green."

News.title: Amazing moment teen who considered amputating his own foot became pain free
News.content:
A teenager who considered amputating his foot because of a rare nerve condition has had a pioneering implant so he can live pain free.

Ralph Seed, 18, has lived with pain in his foot for five years which was so bad that the slightest touch was excruciating, leaving him unable to walk.

He suffers from Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS) but has now become the first teenager in Britain to undergo an operation in the spine to disrupt the nerve signals which register pain in his brain.

There were emotional scenes at Royal Victoria Infirmary in Newcastle when the Inceptiv implant was finally turned on and Ralph’s pain vanished.

‌



View 3 Images Ralph and Dr Rastogi

Pensioner discharged from hospital is in budget hotel for five weeks as rate of bed blocking soars READ MORE :

Dad who campaigned to save SMA babies from lifelong disability tells of new hope READ MORE :

Ralph, from Washington, said: “It was a long journey to get here as the pain has affected my life so much. For the first time in five years, I’m pain free.

“My mum was emotional and so was I. It’s not really hit me, I still can't get my head around it. I’m hoping the implant is going to help me get my life back again.

“I kept going, but I couldn’t plan before as I had to think about how I would cope with pain. Now I am planning my future working with cars and going on a road trip with my family,”

‌



This spinal cord stimulation alters nerve activity by using mild electrical currents to disrupt pain signals before they reach the brain.

Ralph’s doctor, Sachin Rastogi, a consultant anaesthetist at Newcastle Hospitals NHS trust, said: “The results were immediate and unprecedented for a device like this. Seeing the impact of being pain free for Ralph is simply one of the most moving things I have experienced in my career.

View 3 Images Mr Hussain and Dr Rastogi fitting the device in theatre

“This type of closed loop spinal cord stimulation hasn’t been done in the UK before in an adolescent patient with this type of pain. The response has been so dramatic and that is likely to do with his nervous system being young and highly adaptable.”

‌



Ralph first began experiencing discomfort whilst walking, which gradually worsened to the point where he developed a limp. He visited his GP and was referred to A&E where they ran tests and referred Ralph to specialist care.

Ralph underwent MRI and ultrasound scans, surgery to examine his hip, steroid and botox injections, blocks of physiotherapy and hydrotherapy but to no avail. Experts even tried psychological support and pain rehabilitation at the Great North Children’s Hospital, but nothing worked.

By the age of 17 he was experiencing low mood and he began researching amputation of his foot, but was advised by doctors he would have to wait until he was at least 18 to even consider this.

View 3 Images Dr Rastogi and Mr Hussain

‌



Ralph said: “It impacted my life every day. It’s been very hard to do the most basic things as I’ve always been in pain.”

What is Complex Regional Pain Syndrome?

Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS) is when nerves incorrectly send signals to the brain causing severe pain.

It is described as a chronic, severely debilitating pain condition which usually affects a single limb such as an arm, leg, hand or foot.

People with CRPS experience intense pain such as continuous burning, throbbing or aching in the limb. Even a light touch or a mild draft can cause intense pain.

‌



Diagnosing CRPS can be difficult because it involves having tests to rule out other possible causes.

What is Inceptiv implant surgery?

Top neurosurgeon Akbar Hussain placed thin wires near the spinal cord and connected them to a small battery implanted under the skin.

The battery sends gentle electrical pulses to the spinal cord which disrupt or block pain messages, stopping the brain from interpreting them as pain.

‌



Mum Tara Walton, 38, who lives at home in Washington with Ralph, his brother Ernest, 12, and her partner John Walton, 41, said: “It’s really so special to see him smiling again. Ralph has been through so much but throughout he’s had a great attitude, he’s continued to go to school, pushing himself further. He’s been so determined to keep going, showing such resilience passing his GCSEs and going to college.”

The Inceptiv device is ‘closed loop’ meaning it reacts to Ralph’s movement, using the body’s own signals to adapt and adjust the stimulation to meet the patient’s needs.

Similar implants could reduce the effects of Parkinson’s, cut epilepsy seizures and relieve chronic mechanical back pain.

Ralph and his family want to raise awareness of Complex Regional Pain Syndrome. He added: “We want other families who may be going through chronic pain to know about this condition and that there is treatment for it. I’m so thankful to everyone for what they have done for me.”

News.title: UK ranks worst in Europe for mental health, says AXA report
News.content:
UK ranks worst in Europe for mental health, says AXA report

The sixth annual AXA Mind Health Report shows the UK has the worst mental health in Europe and third worst globally, with over one in three people impacted

View 2 Images One in three people in the UK are affected by poor mental health (Image: Getty Images)

The UK has been ranked as having the worst mental health in Europe and the third worst globally - with over one in three people affected by poor mental health, according to worldwide data. Nearly a third of those experiencing mental health difficulties said they are potentially impacted by depression, anxiety or stress at severe or even more extreme levels.

‌



The sixth annual AXA Mind Health Report was carried out by AXA in partnership with Ipsos, surveying 19,000 people aged between 18 and 75 across 18 countries worldwide.

‌



The alarming statistics in this year's report also shed light on the obstacles facing those with mental health issues when seeking support. The figures reveal that 60% haven't visited a mental health professional in the past 12 months, with 25% fearing negative judgement.

‌



It also emerged that almost half (46%) of Brits turn to AI tools for mental health support, though this falls below the global average of 63%. A third (33%) use them to self-manage their mental health, while 42% trust them more than a mental health professional for guidance.

However, opinions on AI-generated mental health advice remain divided – 57% found it helpful, while 43% said they were dissatisfied with the advice they received.

Worryingly, more than a quarter (27%) revealed some AI recommendations led them to engage in harmful behaviour.

‌



View 2 Images Many people are now seeking mental health advice from AI (Image: Getty Images)

Tara Foley, CEO of AXA UK & Ireland said: "It's deeply concerning to see that the UK ranks as having the worst mental health in Europe. These aren't just statistics – the numbers represent real lives and real struggles that deserve our attention and compassion.

"Many people turn to digital tools for help and, while AI can be useful and quick to access, it's no substitute for the empathy and expertise that healthcare professionals provide.

‌



"That's why as a health insurer we provide our members with fast access to mental health support and encourage them to access these services as early as needed, to help prevent people feeling worse or reaching crisis point."

The report uncovers a host of factors taking a toll on mental health, with half of those surveyed pointing to uncertainty about the future in a rapidly evolving world as the greatest concern. Among these changes is the growing use of AI in the workplace.

A separate poll of 2,000 UK adults, carried out by OnePoll.com, examined the impact of AI on the workplace and found that a third are worried about its effect on their career.

Article continues below

A third feel anxious and pessimistic about the use of the tools in the workplace, and are even contemplating changing careers as a result.

Tara Foley added: "Our research reveals that people hold different views on AI in the workplace. While many employees are embracing these time-saving tools, others are equally worried about the impact it may have on their career.

"AI is transforming the way we work and it's important for organisations to help their people develop the skills needed to thrive in this changing environment. Just as important is making sure that employees' mental health and wellbeing is protected and looked after so that everyone feels supported, heard and valued during this transition."

News.title: Oprah Winfrey defends infamous question in Harry and Meghan tell-all chat
News.content:
Oprah Winfrey defends infamous question in Harry and Meghan tell-all chat

Prince Harry and Meghan sat down for a controversial interview with Oprah Winfrey after quitting their royal roles - and the TV host has now spoken out for the first time about the tell-all chat

View 3 Images Oprah Winfrey interviews Prince Harry and Meghan in a controversial tell-all chat (Image: HARPO PRODUCTIONS/AFP via Getty)

Oprah Winfrey has defended one of the most memorable questions from her bombshell tell-all interview with Prince Harry and Meghan.

‌



The highly-anticipated interview saw the Duke and Duchess of Sussex send shockwaves around the world and make several eye-raising allegations about the Royal Family, and how they were treated during their time as senior working royals. One of the most controversial talking points came when they claimed a senior royal raised concerns about the colour of their unborn son Archie's skin.

‌



While in one exchange with Winfrey, Meghan alleged she hadn’t been able to speak up on issues important to her and felt she wasn’t using her voice.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

It prompted the chat show host to ask the now-infamous question: “Were you silent or were you silenced?” And in a new video interview with Vanity Fair, where Winfrey reflects on some of the biggest moments of her career, she watched back on that moment where she asked the question and the hand gesture she performed that went with it.

And she said: “Ok, very nice, I don’t think I’ve done it since. I don’t know where the hell that came from.

‌



“I wanted to be clear because was she silenced, were people telling her not to talk? That’s why I said that. I said it for clarification because I didn’t want later to hear ‘well no it wasn’t that it really was that I was silenced they wouldn’t let me talk. So it was all for clarification’.”

The bombshell interview aired in the US and UK more than five years ago in March 2021, while Meghan was pregnant with Prince Archie and just weeks before the death of the late Prince Philip.

View 3 Images Harry and Meghan's controversial interviewed was aired more than five years ago (Image: Harpo Productions/Joe Pugliese v)

‌



At the time, it forced Buckingham Palace courtiers into crisis talks as they grappled with how to deal with the allegations made against the Firm.

After two days of crisis talks, a statement was issued on behalf of the late Queen that memorably said: “While some recollections may vary, they are taken seriously and will be addressed by the family privately. Harry, Meghan and Archie will always be much-loved family members.”

And reflecting further on the interview and how it was set up, Winfrey added: “This had been postponed probably three times because this was 2021 and I was still in my crazy ‘I can’t leave the house period’ so I didn’t leave the house for 322 days.

‌



“By the time we finally sat down, I think they were both ready. They didn’t know anything I was going to ask them, but I had said to them ahead of time ‘I’m going to try to cover everything’.

View 3 Images Harry and Meghan on a trip to Australia earlier this year (Image: Getty Images)

“This interview took three and a half hours. And is always the case for me, I want it to be a ‘win-win for you’. So I was just trying to carefully go through everything that had come up in the past.” Harry and Meghan’s Oprah interview marked the first of several times the Sussexes rallied against their royal relatives.

‌



Just over a year later, the couple appeared in their Netflix docuseries, where they accused the Firm of lying to protect certain Royal Family members but not them. Months later, Harry also released his memoir Spare, where he accused his brother Prince William of pushing him into a dog bowl in an argument and was highly critical of his stepmother, Queen Camilla.

However, in recent months, Harry has sought to reconcile with his family, including his father, the King, and said in an interview last year that he would love reconciliation with his family.

Earlier this month, Harry brought Meghan and their children to the UK to see the King for the first time in four years. Charles welcomed the Sussexes to his Highgrove residence after days of speculation over whether the family meeting would take place on Harry’s trip to the UK for a series of public appearances.

‌



Archie, seven, and Lilibet, five, had previously seen their grandfather in person during Queen Elizabeth II’s Platinum Jubilee celebrations in 2022.

The meeting between Charles and the young prince and princess is likely to be interpreted as a sign of the thawing of the relationship between the King and his son Harry.

Article continues below

News.title: Police failed to check Manchester synagogue attacker's phones despite arresting him twice
News.content:
A police chief has apologised after admitting phones were twice seized from the Manchester synagogue attacker months before the car and knife assault but they were not examined.

Jihad Al-Shamie, 35, was on bail for an alleged rape when he carried out the attack on Heaton Park Synagogue in Crumpsall on 2 October 2025, in which two Jewish men were killed.

His devices, which contained evidence of his extreme views, were seized after he was arrested in February and September but not analysed.

Greater Manchester Police Chief Constable Sir Stephen Watson said he was "deeply sorry", conceding that "the information contained within these devices would have inspired further investigative action".

Sir Stephen said the end of legal proceedings against Mohammad Bashir, who has been jailed for life with a minimum term of 17 years for plotting a separate attack with Al-Shamie, meant rules around sharing information about a live criminal case had been lifted.

He said: "In conducting an internal review, it became apparent that GMP had seized Al-Shamie's mobile devices, at the point of each arrest.

"The significance of the data contents of these devices was substantial in respect of evidencing an extremist mindset.

"I am disappointed at the prospect of adding to the distress of all of those affected by the terrible events last October.

"For this, I am deeply sorry."

News.title: Gary Lineker among millionaires asking Andy Burnham to tax them more
News.content:
Millionaires including former footballer Gary Lineker and music producer Brian Eno have written to new prime minister Andy Burnham asking to be taxed more.

In an open letter, 120 well-off Britons told Burnham: "We can afford it. We're not talking about higher taxes on those who get up and go to work for their income every day, but on the very richest whose income is derived from the wealth they hold."

Organised by Patriotic Millionaires, the letter said it would lead to a more equal society, and urged a "devolution of wealth and power from the very richest".

People can already give money or stocks voluntarily to the Treasury using a donation facility.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said Lineker is "very welcome to pay more tax he can write a cheque to the Treasury, no one is stopping him."

Patriotic Millionaires support a 2% tax on wealth over Â£10m.

"Millionaires are a patriotic bunch," the letter states. "We love this country and we want it to succeed.

"But success requires investment and a primary source of untouched capital investment is sitting with us, in untaxed potential."

Other signatories include Richard Curtis, director of Notting Hill, and Ian Gregg, the former managing director of Greggs and son of the bakery chain's founder. Scottish crime writer Val McDermid and former financial trader-turned-equality campaigner Gary Stevenson also signed the letter.

Chief Secretary to the Treasury Emma Reynolds said she would welcome UK millionaires increasing the amount of tax they pay but said any major changes would be announced during a Budget.

"I welcome the fact that people of good means are saying that they want to pay more. They can pay more," she said and pointed to the Treasury's donation link.

The renewed call for higher tax on the wealthy follows a similar campaign in previous years.

Burnham did not rule out a wealth tax when asked about it by Lineker - formerly the BBC's highest paid presenter - a few days before he became prime minister.

He suggested he may have "to ask for a little more" tax at some point.

Lineker was paid around Â£1.3m a year before he left the BBC. He is worth a reported Â£30m.

The latest call from Patriotic Millionaires said there is a "need to embrace a new kind of devolution of wealth and power, from the very richest in order to reinvest back into our greatest asset in every region".

It added that in its own poll, the majority of millionaires wanted a higher tax on themselves.

"There are a few people left with outdated economic thinking and few others desperate to hold onto every penny they can... Those that can't see past the end of their own self interest have no place in designing a Britain for the future," the letter said.

Musician Brian Eno told BBC Radio Lincolnshire the tax system was "very generous to rich people".

"If you're wealthy you don't pay very much tax but hire a clever bunch of accountants who somehow get you off that," he said.

He also dismissed the idea that lots of millionaires would leave the UK if they were taxed too much.

"That is the story that has always been told by the rich to avoid this but in fact people don't leave that much.

"Of course a few people will," he said, but added that people don't necessarily leave other high-tax countries, such as those in Scandinavia.

He insisted most of his financial peers do want to see better roads and schools and that they don't like seeing people living in extreme poverty, and that many financially support community groups.

News.title: Police officer was violent rapist who attacked women over 14 years, BBC reveals
News.content:
A police officer who took his own life in May was a violent rapist who carried out attacks and attempted murders of women over at least 14 years, the BBC can reveal.

PC Alan Greer's first known victim was a woman he raped in her home in Glasgow in 2012 after she had called the police to report being the victim of a crime.

The woman reported the sex attack by Greer late last year, sparking one of Police Scotland's biggest ever anti-corruption inquiries.

Detectives have so far uncovered a further eight victims, five of whom were sex workers, attacked while Greer was off duty.

It has emerged that Greer used hundreds of prostitutes throughout his police career, and it is anticipated more victims of his violence will be identified.

Assistant Chief Constable Lynn Ratcliff, gold commander for the investigation, said what the inquiry had found was "truly shocking".

She said: "This officer has clearly abused his power and has revisited someone that he's encountered in the course of his duties.

"But this victim was brave enough to come and speak to us, and that really was the trigger point for us starting our investigation.

"That's allowed us to proactively identify eight further victims."

News.title: Airport drop-off fees up by a third - here are the priciest
News.content:
Drop-off fees at the UK's major airports have risen by a third on average since last summer, new analysis has found.

The RAC motoring group looked at the cost of pulling up to the closest point to terminals at the 20 busiest airports, 16 of which had put up their prices since last year.

London airport Gatwick topped the list by charging a "farewell fee" of Â£10 for 10 minutes, after lifting it by Â£3 from last year. Stansted also charges Â£10 but drivers are allowed 15 minutes at its "express set down" outside departures.

Airports UK, the trade body, said that free drop-offs were available and fees were part of airports' business models and climate change objectives.

The RAC said that the price of dropping people off in "kiss-and-fly" areas rose by an average of Â£1.70 to Â£7 compared to this time last year.

London City Airport, which only started making people pay this year, is the most expensive on a per-minute basis. Its Â£8 charge for five minutes works out at Â£1.60 per minute.

There have been increases in Northern Ireland too. At Belfast International Airport, it is now Â£5 for 10 minutes in the drop-off zone, up Â£2 on last year.

In contrast, none of the top 10 airports in the EU charge for drop-offs, according to RAC research.

News.title: 'Every victim will feel the same,' says mother of PC Harper over early prison release
News.content:
The mother of PC Andrew Harper has said her son has not been given "proper justice" and "every victim will be feeling the same" about the early prison release scheme.

PC Harper, 28, was killed in 2019 when he was dragged by a car down a country road as three teenagers fled the scene of a quad bike theft in Berkshire.

Under the Sentencing Act, which is due to be implemented in September, two of the men involved could be freed early.

As the deadline for releases approaches, Andy Burnham has reignited a row over the legislation after he said he would review the plans.

But, two prison staffers told the BBC that governors were told to stop work on the implementation of the Sentencing Act two weeks ago. The government maintains there has been no decision to delay its introduction.

PC Harper's mother, Debbie Adlam, said the release of Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers - two of the passengers in the getaway car which killed Harper - was "sprung" on her family.

Cole and Bowers - who were 17 at the time - were sentenced to 13 years in custody for manslaughter but could be released after six years under the act.

The driver of the car, Henry Long - who was 18 - was jailed for 16 years for manslaughter but would not be eligible for early release.

"It just feels like another let down for Andrew really, when you look at the horrific way he was killed, we have to live with that," she told BBC Radio 4's Today Programme.

"The feeling that Andrew hasn't been given proper justice, it is very personal obviously... every victim will be feeling the same."

The Sentencing Act is the government's attempt to find a permanent, more sustainable solution to a prison overcrowding crisis after an emergency scheme was introduced by the Labour government in 2024.

Tens of thousands of inmates have already been let out of prison early under those measures.

Unlike the 2024 plan, the new act includes no exemptions for prisoners convicted of serious crimes, domestic abuse or terrorism.

News.title: Johnson-Thompson and Asher-Smith out of Commonwealths
News.content:
England's Olympic 800m champion Keely Hodgkinson had already skipped the event to prioritise the European Championships, which begin in Birmingham on 10 August, leading many to question the event's significance in the sporting calendar.

The squad for the European Championships is expected to be announced next week.

St Lucia's 100m Olympic champion Julien Alfred has also pulled out of the Glasgow Games, while Canadian swimmer Summer McIntosh, one of the sport's biggest stars, is favouring the Pan Pacific Swimming Championships.

With the likes of the United States, China and major European nations not part of the Commonwealths, some athletes favour other, more competitive events.

These Games were also hurt by the late confirmation of its dates and schedule, which only came in October last year. The event was originally scheduled for March, but the Australian state of Victoria pulled out as hosts in 2023.

Speaking on Thursday, organisers insisted the event would be a success despite the absence of some big names.

Scottish athletics medal hopes include new mile world record holder Josh Kerr and defending 10,000m champion Eilish McColgan, while Glasgow 2026 chief executive Phil Batty said focus should be on younger athletes.

"We have got an incredible field of athletes," he said.

"It is really important to make sure we have those athletes at the pinnacle of their career and you can see that across the sports.

"It is equally exciting to see, just like what happened in 2014 [previous Glasgow Games], which athletes this starts that breakthrough moment."

Commonwealth Sport chief executive Katie Sadlier said her organisation would have conversations with other events in the future to create a clearer window.

"This Games was a little bit of a challenge because we only had 18 months and it was really difficult to say 'where is the gap in the two-year period?'.

"As we move forward more of those conversations will happen."

News.title: Rain to return this weekend as parts of UK on brink of drought
News.content:
If you cannot remember the last time it rained, you are probably not alone.

June was actually wetter than average in the UK, which might come as a surprise given our recent run of weather, but for England and Wales the majority of that rain came down in the first two weeks of the month.

Since 15 June, most of England has recorded less than 10mm of rain with large areas of central southern England seeing 3mm or less. Meanwhile, Wisley in Surrey has had no rain at all for 36 consecutive days.

Most of Wales has seen less than 25mm (1in) of rain since the middle of June, but it has been particularly dry in the north-east with Rhyl in Denbighshire recording only 3mm.

A Thames Water hosepipe ban came into force on Thursday, adding to other bans already in place for customers of other water companies across the south of the UK, as parts of southern, central and eastern England were declared to be close to drought.

Northern Ireland had a very wet June, recording 67% more rain than average, and it was also very wet in western Scotland. However, July has been much drier than average in Northern Ireland and most of Scotland, though the rain has continued in the Highlands, with Aultbea already reaching the July average rainfall, and with more on the way.

News.title: Liquor store employee narrowly escapes leopard attack
News.content:
CCTV footage showed the moment a leopard entered a liquor store and attacked a salesman in Rajasthan, north western India.

Earlier, the animal had already attacked a cleaning worker inside.

Afterwards, the leopard hid near the counter so both employees managed to escape.

Others helped shut the shop, trapping the leopard inside.

After nearly five hours, officials tranquillised and captured the animal.

It was later released back into the wild, local authorities confirmed.

Reporting by Mohar Singh Meena and Purushottam Joshi of BBC News Hindi

News.title: Shapps blocked from standing again for the Conservatives
News.content:
Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has told the BBC she leads "a brand new party full of new people" - after it emerged in the Spectator, external that the former cabinet minister and Tory party chairman Sir Grant Shapps has been rejected as a Conservative Party parliamentary candidate.

Sir Grant, who has declined to comment, served in nine ministerial roles in government as well as co-chairing the party.

In cabinet, he served as home secretary, defence secretary, transport secretary, business secretary, energy secretary and net zero secretary.

He was also a Foreign Office Minister, housing minister and international development minister, external.

He lost his Welwyn Hatfield seat to Labour's Andrew Lewin in 2024 by 3,799 votes after representing it since 2005.

But his application to stand again for the Conservatives at the next general election has been declined.

One party source told the BBC "it reflects badly on Kemi's temperament. North Korean purges don't work in British politics".

Badenoch told a news conference in central London: "We don't treat our former MPs or our candidates like tittle-tattle for Westminster gossip.

"What I will say is that we're going to be announcing candidates shortly, and you will see that this is a very different party from the one that was removed from government in 2024."

News.title: 'Life-changing' MS drug to help people walk now on NHS in England
News.content:
The first drug to help people with multiple sclerosis walk is being made available on the NHS in England.

Fampridine boosts nerve signals to make it easier for some people to move and live independently.

Aysen Slack, who used to pay for fampridine privately until it became too costly, said the decision would make a "huge difference".

Up to 5,000 people in England could benefit each year. The drug is already available elsewhere in the UK.

Multiple sclerosis is caused by the immune system attacking the protective covering around nerve cells - known as myelin.

This damage impairs the ability of nerves to carry electrical messages from the brain to the rest of the body - including those needed for the precise control of muscles needed to walk.

Fampridine is known as a "signal booster" as it helps those electrical messages still get through.

Clinical trials showed around four in 10 people taking the drug had improvements in their walking speed and in how long they could walk for.

This could be the difference between getting around the house or needing help at home or enabling people to go out and see friends and family.

Current NHS support includes physiotherapy and walking aids.

The drug has previously been rejected for use by the NHS in England as it was not considered value for money, although it did become available in Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.

News.title: Love Island: All Stars winners Molly Smith and Tom Clare marry
News.content:
Sharing more from their marriage ceremony, Molly posted a photo to her Instagram story of her hand on top of Tom's.

The snap showed their wedding rings along with a bouquet of flowers, with the caption: "Husband and wife".

The couple first got together two years ago, when they met on season one of Love Island: All Stars.

All Stars is a spin-off of the hit dating show, which sees past contestants return for a second chance at finding love in the villa.

During the reality dating show, the pair beat Molly's ex-boyfriend Callum Jones and his partner at the time, Jessica Gale, who finished as runners-up.

Molly previously starred in series six in 2020 and left the show with Callum, who she was in a relationship with for three years before they split.

While Hyde United footballer Tom previously came third place on the second winter edition of Love Island in 2023 with former partner Samie Elishi.

Earlier this year, Tom and Molly took over hosting duties of the NearlyWeds podcast from radio presenters and reality stars Jamie Laing and Sophie Habboo.

Fellow Love Island stars were among those to congratulate the couple, including former winner Casey O'Gorman who described it as the "best day".

Sophie Piper, who came third on their All Star season, and TikTok star GK Barry also shared their support with the newly weds.

News.title: Ex-Coronation Street actor to receive 'substantial' libel damages from the Sun publisher
News.content:
Former Coronation Street actor Qasim Akhtar is to receive "substantial" damages from the Sun's publisher, to settle a High Court libel claim.

Akhtar who played Zeedan Nazir in the ITV soap from 2014 to 2018 and then 2021 to 2023, sued News Group Newspapers (NGN) earlier this year.

A story in the Sun had falsely alleged Akhtar had "backed" and "teamed up with" Islamic cleric Uthman ibn Farooq, was associated with extremism, radicalisation and violence, and had "moved to Pakistan" and "trained with guns".

The newspaper previously apologised "unreservedly" to the actor for the "serious harm and distress caused to him by the publication of these false allegations".

The story, published in November, appeared in The Sun online and in print.

The Manchester-born actor, who has previously appeared in TV shows including Shameless and Waterloo Road, did not attend the court proceedings.

But his lawyer, Daniel Taylor, read out an agreed statement, saying NGN had agreed to pay "substantial damages" and Akhtar's legal costs.

"The defendant has accepted that the publication of the article caused serious harm to Mr Akhtar's reputation and also caused him great distress," he said.

"This included reputational harm to his family life and business, which he was forced to put on hold pending the matter being resolved.

"The libel was compounded by the fact that the defendant has acknowledged that it failed to obtain Mr Akhtar's response to these very serious allegations prior to publication."

News.title: Bonnie Tyler's funeral to be broadcast online to fans around the world
News.content:
Fans around the world will be able to watch a celebration of life service for Welsh singer Bonnie Tyler in an online broadcast.

The Total Eclipse of the Heart singer died "unexpectedly" on 8 July, aged 75, at a Portugal hospital, "as a result of the illness that she was being treated for", her family said.

The service for family and invited guests will be held at St Mary's Church, Swansea, on 17 August, and will be live streamed on the star's official website.

The cortege will then travel to her hometown of Skewen, Neath Port Talbot, travelling through the village at about 13:20 BST, an update on the website, external said.

Fans will also be able to watch the service on television screens outside the church, the update said.

Before that, her coffin will be brought to her Mumbles home on 15 August at 15:30 BST, with people invited to "pay their respects" by lining Newton Road at 15:15.

Tyler, born Gaynor Hopkins - also known for hits including Holding Out For A Hero and Here She Comes - is survived by her husband of more than 50 years, Robert Sullivan.

Oscar-winning actress and Wednesday star Catherine Zeta-Jones led the tributes to Bonnie Tyler earlier this month, saying her heart was "broken" with the news that "our dearest Bonnie Tyler has passed away".

The Prince of Wales described Tyler as a "proud Welsh icon" and Sir Cliff Richard said he was mourning "another wonderful friend gone too soon".

In May, Tyler was placed into an induced coma after having emergency intestinal surgery in Portugal.

Last month, her spokesperson said she was out of the coma but remained "very unwell and in intensive care".

Total Eclipse of the Heart, her biggest hit, topped the charts on both sides of the Atlantic.

In doing so, she became the first Welsh person to score a number one hit in the US.

News.title: Girl 'youngest' to have conscious brain surgery for condition
News.content:
A teenager has become the world's youngest known patient to have brain surgery to treat a particular blood vessel abnormality, hospital bosses have said.

Tilly Phillips, now 16, was 15 when she underwent the conscious craniotomy procedure at Alder Hey Children's Hospital in Liverpool.

The 12-hour procedure was to resolve an arteriovenous malformation, which is an abnormal tangle of blood vessels that causes seizures and can be fatal.

Tilly, from Warrington, Cheshire, said the condition had felt like a "ticking time bomb" and that her life had been "on hold".

As well as causing seizures, the abnormality was also close to areas of the brain controlling speech, movement and vision.

Surgeons woke Tilly for about 30 minutes so they could map those parts of her brain in real time and protect vital tissue while removing the malformation.

Although she cannot remember being conscious, the medical team said she was coherent and calmly completed picture-naming tasks.

Clinical psychologist Cathy Grant said electrical stimulation briefly stopped Tilly from naming objects, helping surgeons identify tissue that needed to be protected.

Tilly said she thought the sedation and memory problems she experienced afterwards might explain why she could not recall being awake.

News.title: Marathon runners compete on drifting sea ice at North Pole
News.content:
Twenty-three runners from seven countries took part in races at the Arctic's geographic North Pole, organisers have said, in an event they dubbed as the "world's coolest marathon".

The races took place on drifting sea ice at the geographic North Pole in the Arctic, with competitors arriving from Norway aboard the French polar vessel Le Commandant Charcot.

They disembarked the ship to run laps of a 1,055 metre loop on the ice below, wearing thermal gear and life vests as a safety requirement, while armed guards kept watch for polar bears around the perimeter.

Denmark's Rikke Dam won the women's title with a time of 6:54:02 and Wang Shengxian of China won the men's race in 3:52:22. Organisers said the course disappeared with the ice just hours after the races ended.

Video edited by Ian Aikman

News.title: 'A 10-goal thriller': England fans react to 6-4 win over France
News.content:
England supporters in Miami have been celebrating the team finishing third in the World Cup, after victory over France. The win secured England's best-placed finish in the tournament since lifting the trophy in 1966.

Three Lions fans were left disappointed when England lost their semi-final with Argentina on Wednesday, failing to secure a spot in Sunday's final at the New York New Jersey Stadium.

However, England fans who stayed with the team for the match with France were treated to a thrilling 10-goal match.

England dominated the first half to lead 4-0, but France's resurgence in the second half saw the Three Lions edge out a 6-4 victory.

News.title: Manchester synagogue terrorist’s phones revealed his extremist views – but police failed to check them
News.content:

Read our Privacy notice

The Manchester synagogue terrorist’s phones revealed he held extremist views, but police failed to check them when they seized them months earlier after his arrest for other alleged crimes.

Greater Manchester Police (GMP) Chief Constable Sir Stephen Watson said there is “little doubt” that the information contained on his phones would have inspired further investigative action, and admitted it was a “missed opportunity” and that the data on the phones would have pointed towards Jihad Al-Shamie’s extremist mindset.

Al-Shamie, 35, was on bail at the time for an alleged rape, leading police to seize his devices as part of their investigation. He was shot dead by police as he targeted the place of worship in Heaton Park on Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar, last year.

Melvin Cravitz, 66, and Adrian Daulby, 53, died after what police and government leaders condemned as a “vile” terrorist attack.

Sir Stephen said the failure had come to light after an internal investigation by GMP, adding he is “deeply sorry” for the “added distress” for the families of those who died.

open image in gallery Jihad Al-Shamie ( Facebook )

“In conducting an internal review, it became apparent that GMP had seized Al-Shamie’s mobile devices, at the point of each arrest. The significance of the data contents of these devices was substantial in respect of evidencing an extremist mindset,” he said.

“Regrettably, I can confirm that the significance of the information stored on Al-Shamie’s devices was not realised as they had not been examined before the attack took place on the 2nd of October 2025.”

Sir Stephen added it was “clear” that the failure to review the devices was a “missed opportunity”: “There can however, be little doubt that the information contained within these devices would have inspired further investigative action. It is clear that our not having reviewed the data available to us prior to the attack constitutes a missed opportunity.

“I am disappointed at the prospect of adding to the distress of all of those affected by the terrible events last October. For this, I am deeply sorry.”

open image in gallery Mohammad Bashir, an associate of Al-Shamie, was jailed for life on Thursday ( Greater Manchester Police )

It comes after Mohammad Bashir, an associate of Al-Shamie, was jailed for life on Thursday for planning a mass attack of his own.

Detectives found he had shared voicenotes and messages containing extremist Islamic content with Al-Shamie, and that the pair had travelled together to the UK Defence Academy (UKDA) on a reconnaissance mission to plan an attack.

Seven weeks later, Al-Shamie chose the alternative target for the attack he carried out alone, while Bashir was in Pakistan. Bashir was quickly identified as an associate and arrested upon his return to the UK.

Sir Stephen said he was able to share the information regarding the missed opportunities following the conclusion of legal proceedings against Bashir.

He added the forthcoming inquests into the deaths of the two men murdered by Al-Shamie at the synagogue will examine “all aspects of the attack” and the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) is also conducting a review.

He said it is for the IOPC and the coroner to determine the “impact” of police not reviewing the contents of Al-Shamie’s devices before the attack took place.

The mother and daughter who died after getting into difficulty in the water off the Essex coast have been named as Shally Rahman, 42, and Samiha Rahman, 15.

A seven-year-old boy is also in a serious condition in hospital, the family told the BBC.

Emergency services were called to West Mersea beach near Colchester at 5:35pm on Wednesday evening. Witnesses reported seeing a group of people standing on a seabank as the tide came in, and described them “calling for help”.

Paramedics said one patient was transported by air to hospital, and a further three patients were transported by road to hospital.

Detective Chief Inspector Al Pitcher said: "Today, our thoughts remain with the family members who are coming to terms with their loss.

"We are grateful to the people who have already spoken to us and helped with our enquiries. We would ask anyone who was at the beach at the time, and who has not yet spoken with officers, to please get in touch, to help us understand what happened.”

He added: ”At this stage of our enquiries, we believe those involved in the incident knew each other. Anyone who was in the area at the time and has information or footage which may assist our investigation is asked to contact us on 101 and quote incident 1090.”

A newlywed Wisconsin couple quickly put their “in sickness and in health” vows to the test when the bride’s severe stomach illness landed her in the emergency room during their honeymoon.

Gretchen Pleuss said she contracted Cyclospora, the parasite linked to a 41-state outbreak that has sickened thousands, during her honeymoon camping trip to Yellowstone National Park, turning what should have been a celebration into a medical ordeal.

“It was just like incessant diarrhea, so just like watery and constant,” Pleuss told WISN about her illness. “I felt fine until we got out here, and then a couple days into camping into the Badlands, I started having symptoms.”

The agony eventually grew too intense to ignore, forcing Pleuss to make a pitstop at the emergency room. Doctors determined she had the Cyclospora parasite in her system, which Pleuss believes she got from shredded lettuce in a sandwich.

“It feels like your intestines are really tight, like something is seizing them,” Pleuss, who is being treated with antibiotics, said about her pain.

A Wisconsin woman said she landed in the ER during her Yellowstone honeymoon after contracting Cyclospora ( Getty Images )

Despite the rough start, Pleuss said the couple is still trying to enjoy their vacation.

“It’s still our honeymoon, so we’re making the best of it. Our vows said, ‘In sickness and in health,’ so we’re just getting an early start on that,” Pleuss joked.

Since May 1, the U.S. has recorded 4,173 laboratory-confirmed Cyclospora cases across 41 states, with health officials investigating more than 7,400 additional reported infections, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said Tuesday. The outbreak has hospitalized 308 people, though no deaths have been reported.

The main symptoms of a Cyclospora infection include watery diarrhea, fatigue and loss of appetite. Most people start feeling sick about a week after being exposed, though symptoms can appear anywhere from two days to more than two weeks later, according to the CDC.

The outbreak has been linked to shredded iceberg lettuce, prompting Taylor Farms de Mexico to voluntarily recall all iceberg lettuce sourced from central Mexico after the FDA traced the illnesses to what the company said is a single farm that supplies less than 1 percent of the U.S. iceberg lettuce market.

The recalled lettuce was distributed to Taco Bell restaurants linked to the multistate outbreak. The chain has since removed Taylor Farms lettuce from its locations.

The FDA continues to urge consumers not to eat the recalled Taylor Farms iceberg lettuce, saying there's strong evidence linking a separate batch of the lettuce to the Cyclospora outbreak.

The warning remains in place even though a lab test that initially detected the parasite in one sample was determined to be a false positive over the weekend.

News.content:
