Scientists at a U.S.-funded facility in Panama are preparing to launch the first outdoor tests of genetically modified screwworm flies, a significant step in developing a more effective weapon against the flesh-eating parasite that has spread through Central America and into the United States.

Researchers will confine the flies in mesh cages, exposing them to Panama's heat and humidity. This aims to measure their survival outside laboratory conditions before advancing to later stages of field testing.

The Trump administration has touted the genetically modified fly, named NovoFly, as a game-changer in the fight against New World screwworm. Widespread infestations could cause estimated losses exceeding $1 billion to Texas' livestock industry and threaten other U.S. states.

Screwworms are parasitic flies whose females lay eggs in open wounds and mucous membranes on warm-blooded animals. Once hatched, hundreds of larvae use sharp mouths to burrow through living flesh, eventually killing their host if untreated.

For decades, the most effective tool was widespread dispersal of sterile screwworm flies, mostly produced at the Panama facility. The U.S. Department of Agriculture and Panama's Ministry of Agricultural Development jointly manage this plant, opened in 2006, intended to maintain a barrier against wild screwworms moving north.

open image in gallery NovoFly is a screwworm fly genetically engineered to produce only males. Once these male offspring are sterilized, they can be released to mate with wild female screwworm flies, which then lay unfertilized eggs ( REUTERS )

However, wild screwworm flies have now spread throughout Mexico and, in June, infested Texas farms for the first time in decades. With cases over a large area, the 100 million sterile flies produced weekly in Panama are insufficient. Experts say 500 million a week are needed to push the parasite back to the Darien Gap, the rainforest between Panama and Colombia.

Enter NovoFly, a screwworm fly genetically engineered to produce only males. Once these male offspring are sterilized, they can be released to mate with wild female screwworm flies, which then lay unfertilized eggs.

Wild female screwworms typically mate only once, so sterile male flies can progressively decline the population until eradication. The USDA began using this technique in 1957, eradicating the pest from the United States by 1966, and using it for later outbreaks.

The NovoFly project aims to boost sterile fly production. Currently, the Panama facility produces both males and females. Females are useless in controlling wild populations, but separating them is difficult, according to the USDA and entomologists.

"It's going to allow us to almost instantaneously double the number of sterile flies that we put in the fight," Scott Hutchins, USDA's chief scientist and an undersecretary, said at a June news conference. "It's going to give us a tremendous edge."

The USDA conducts some screwworm research at the Knipling-Bushland U.S. Livestock Insects Research Laboratory in Kerrville, Texas, named after entomologists who developed the sterilization process. Flies are blasted with radiation before release, a process also for NovoFly.

Officials at the Kerrville lab told Reuters on an exclusive tour that scientists expect imminent approval from Panama's biosecurity agency to begin NovoFly tests outdoors at the Panama lab.

The Panama-United States Commission for the Eradication and Prevention of Screwworm (COPEG), which operates the Panama plant, deferred information requests to the USDA. The Panamanian Food Agency declined to comment.

SUCCESS NOT GUARANTEED

The outdoor testing is critical to determining the potential effectiveness of the NovoFly. Scientists do not know whether it will have the strength and virility to fly far enough to find and attract wild mates.

After the initial tests in Panama, larger field trials on NovoFly are expected to begin at a ranch nearby in nine to 12 weeks, when researchers will release 50,000 of the insects every few days, said Alex Arp, a USDA research geneticist working in Panama. The flies will be marked with fluorescent dyes visible under black light, and traps around the ranch will allow researchers to track how long each release survives, he said.

open image in gallery Wild screwworm flies have now spread throughout Mexico and, in June, infested Texas farms for the first time in decades ( Getty Images )

Field tests typically run for about six to eight weeks, said Maxwell Scott, an entomologist at North Carolina State University who helped develop NovoFly, warning that success was not guaranteed: "We may get out in the field, and it may not fly very well."

If NovoFly performs well in trials, it would take time to scale up production, according to the USDA. Rather than producing NovoFly initially in Panama, it may be less risky to do it at a new sterile-fly production facility expected to open in Texas late next year, experts said.

Adding NovoFly to the facility in Panama could risk disrupting the largest source of sterile flies and a collapse of production, if scientists fail to establish the correct diets, temperatures and conditions for the new strain.

"The last thing we'd want to do is rush a process to be able to have what's called a total brood collapse," said Rear Admiral Michael Schmoyer, who is leading USDA's efforts against screwworm, at a legislative hearing in Texas. "You start with zero, and then you have to build up again."

The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency published a proposed decision to register NovoFly in June, according to the USDA. If fully approved, NovoFly would become the first genetically modified insect to get full EPA clearance, Scott said.

Even a modest increase in the number of sterilized males could lead to a quicker eradication of wild screwworm flies, said Edwin Burgess, an assistant professor of veterinary entomology at the University of Florida who is not involved in the project. However, researchers need to make sure NovoFly is competitive against wild male screwworm flies for mating and can be reared successfully on a large scale, he said.

"There are still a lot of things that need to be done to get that technology to where it needs to be," Burgess said. "But it's certainly very, very promising."

Mexico supports using the male-only flies and could be producing them by the end of the year at a newly reopened production plant, said Gabriel Ayala, head of animal health for Mexico's National Service for Agri-Food Health, Safety and Quality. Eventually, they could be produced in Panama, Mexico and at the planned U.S. plant in Texas, he said.

Kerrville lab director Kim Lohmeyer said she hopes the U.S. can eradicate screwworms much faster than the decades it took before the pests were controlled in the 1960s. But, even if the NovoFly trials succeed and it is brought into production, it will likely take more than a year to control the pest, she said.

"It will take some time and effort," she said. "We need more flies."

American chat show host Jimmy Fallon has taken aim at the state of UK politics, mocking Andy Burnham becoming the newest prime minister in a skit – however, many Brits aren’t seeing the funny side.

In a sketch onThe Tonight Show with Jimmy Fallon, the US comic mocked the fact that Brits have witnessed seven prime ministers enter No. 10 Downing Street over the last decade. Speaking to the audience, Fallon said: “The UK just appointed their seventh new prime minister in only 10 years and now here to talk about it is the new prime minister, Andy Burnham. Andy, thank you for being here.”

The show then cut to a tall man in glasses in front of the prime ministerial residence, whose similarities with Burnham appeared to stop there as he then said in a plummy English accent: “Thanks for having me Jimmy. I’m thrilled to serve both King and country in this new role.”

open image in gallery An actor playing Andy Burnham in a 'Tonight Show' skit ( The Tonight Show with Jimmy Fallon )

After cutting back to Fallon, who asked what the first item of his agenda as country leader would be, a completely different person was seen standing in Burnham’s place, saying: “Great question, Jimmy.”

“I’m sorry, what’s going on? What happened to Andy? The prime minister,” a confused Fallon asked, to which the new leader replied: “Oh, he’s no longer prime minister. I am – Nigel Remmington.”

The same gag repeated throughout the skit, with different, generic British politicians replacing one another before a frustrated Fallon asked: “Can you guys just pick someone and stick to it? Isn’t there someone in the UK who everyone likes?”

It’s at that point that Harry Potter’s Albus Dumbledore showed up as the new prime minister. “You’re not even a real guy,” Fallon asked, to which the white-bearded wizard responded: “It was either me or Meghan Markle,” before – *checks notes* – dabbing.

open image in gallery Prime Minister Andy Burnham was appointed Prime Minister on 20 July ( Getty )

Unsurprisingly, many Brits didn’t take too kindly to the skit – particularly the impression of Burnham. “At least give Burnham a northern accent ffs,” one viewer wrote on X, while another said: “Why did Burnham a southern accent? The guys main thing is hes the northern one.”

“F*** it’s unfunny but it’s annoyingly accurate,” a third wrote. While a fourth tweeted: “Very funny,” with a GIF of a lego figure dying from “cringe”.

Others heaped praise on the show however, with one writing on YouTube: “As an Englishman, I just want to say that this is completely accurate.” Another said: “UK skit is truer to life than reality.”

Labour prime minister Burnham is famously from Lancashire and an MP for Makerfield in Greater Manchester, having previously been the city’s mayor for nine years. He’s vowed to move more country-running operations up north, pledging to create an outpost of Downing Street based in Manchester.

Earlier this year, Burnham was portrayed by comedian Paddy Young on Saturday Night Live UK in a sketch where various Labour party members tried to oust Keir Starmer out of No. 10 and move in. Bursting into the residence with a bindle over his shoulder, Young’s Burnham announced that he had taken “the tram down” from Manchester.

Last month, Fallon faced backlash after interviewing Irish mixed martial arts fighter Conor McGregor following his 2024 sexual assault trial – with actor Christina Ricci sharing a post which read: “Why the absolute f*** is this piece of human garbage being given a platform on Jimmy Fallon’s show? Shame on you, Jimmy.”

Jason Alexander has apologized to Courtney Stodden for an inappropriate sketch from 2012 that resurfaced, but Stodden wants him to turn his words into action.

Stodden called out Alexander in a Monday Instagram post, reflecting on a dated Funny or Die comedy sketch in which the Seinfeld star — who was 52 at the time — rubbed his phone on a 17-year-old Stodden’s breast and told her that when she turned 18, he would “have his way” with her.

Alexander, now 66, said in a statement to TMZ: “Looking back at the comedy sketch in which Ms. Stodden and I participated in 2012, I completely agree that it was inappropriate and I truly regret it. But more importantly, I am deeply sorry for any harm or distress it has caused Ms. Stodden. I offer my sincerest apologies.”

In response to Alexander’s apology, Stodden told Variety that she appreciated the actor taking responsibility — but pleaded with him to advocate for change against child exploitation.

“I’m very taken aback that an adult was actually able to take accountability because I haven’t heard a lot of adults take accountability,” Stodden, now 31, explained to the outlet.

Courtney Stodden has urged Jason Alexander to speak out against laws that allow children to get married ( Getty/NBC )

“When I first got word that he publicly apologized I was grateful because I think that’s the first step in change,” she continued. “At the same time, I think it would be even better if he put that into action, so I would urge Jason Alexander to support AB 1267 and support what’s happening in California or even donate to Unchained at Last.”

AB 1267 refers to a proposed California bill that proposes to end child marriage by setting the state’s minimum marriage age to 18 with no exceptions.

At the time that the sketch, titled “The Don Clay Show with Courtney Stodden,” aired, Stodden was married to Green Mile actor Doug Hutchison.

They had famously tied the knot when she was just 16 and he was 51. They were together from 2011 to 2018, and Stodden has since advocated against minors getting married.

“I was a minor,” Stodden said in her Instagram post. “I didn’t have the legal power to decide whether I wanted to participate. The contracts were signed by adults. The paycheck went to Doug. The production moved forward. I was the only child in the room. I felt so alone.”

She continued: “Legally, I couldn’t make those decisions for myself. That’s the point. I can’t change what happened to me but I can ask myself: How did so many adults look at a minor and decide this was acceptable? That’s exactly why I speak out today. Children deserve laws that protect them. They shouldn’t have to become adults before realizing the law should have protected them all along.”

The police shooting death of a man who injured an officer with a knife while resisting arrest has roiled the city of Madison, Wisconsin, with Gov. Tony Evers calling for “transparency and accountability” in any investigation and community members gathering at a growing memorial for the man.

Protesters marched Wednesday after the shooting and held a candlelight vigil for the man who died. Some even stayed at the growing memorial of candles, flowers and signs overnight, like Ben Weger.

“I don't plan to leave anytime soon because it's important to hold this space,” said Weger, pastor of Stoughton United Methodist Church about 20 miles (32 kilometers) away.

Sabrina Thompsen, of Madison, was crying at the memorial site. “It’s really unbearable,” she said. “You can’t describe it.”

Evers posted online saying, “We will continue to keep the loved ones and family of the individual who was killed in our hearts and prayers.”

“His life mattered,” the governor said.

Cellphone video of the confrontation, where three gunshots could be heard, circulated on social media.

Madison Police Chief John Patterson stressed at a news conference that the online footage was just one perspective of what happened.

“I want to take a moment to honestly and sincerely offer my heartfelt sympathies to his family for this loss,” Patterson said. The man killed was in his 30s, Patterson said, but police did not release his name.

Patterson said police were responding to calls that someone was attempting to enter parked vehicles in the neighborhood. The suspect fled on a bike in an attempt to get away before officers contacted him in the street.

The suspect either fell off his bike or was taken off his bike by officers, Patterson said. During the struggle, the suspect pulled out a knife and injured an officer. An officer deployed a taser but it was unsuccessful. The same officer who was injured by the knife fired his weapon and the man who was shot died later at the hospital. The chief described the officer who fired his weapon as a veteran officer, but did not reveal any other details.

Another officer was injured, but it is not clear how, Patterson said. Two other officers who were involved were uninjured.

The Wisconsin Department of Criminal Investigation will investigate the shooting, and the four officers will be placed on administrative leave.

“There are questions that must be answered,” Madison Mayor Satya Rhodes-Conway posted online. “It’s understandable that people want answers now.”

The shooting happened on a city street in a popular neighborhood lined with restaurants, bars, shops and residential homes less than 2 miles (3.2 kilometers) from the state Capitol. Footage shows numerous cars stopped in the intersection with people watching as it unfolded.

A white police officer shot and killed Tony Robinson, who was biracial, on the same street in 2015; a shooting that spurred large protests. The district attorney did not file charges against police in that case, determining the officer was justified.

The race of the officer who fired his gun on Wednesday and that of the man killed were not released by police.

But Black advocacy groups in Madison quickly spoke out against the crime and said they believed the man was Black.

“Another Black man is dead on a Madison street, and our community watched him die before we even knew his name,” said Brandi Grayson, the head of the Madison-based Black community advocacy group Urban Triage. “That is the cruelty of state violence.”

The shooting quickly infused itself into the Democratic race for governor, with one candidate addressing mourners at the site of the vigil Wednesday night and others calling for swift investigations.

“I am horrified and devastated,” posted Francesca Hong, who showed up at the scene just a few blocks from her campaign office.

Another candidate, County Executive David Crowley, said while details of what happened are still needed, “these reports are painfully reminiscent of the tragedies we have witnessed in Kenosha, Minneapolis, and far too many communities across our country.”

A crowd had formed near where the shooting occurred on Wednesday with people chanting, “Arrest the cops!” They placed flowers and candles where the man was shot.

Protesters also marched to the state Capitol and took the stage at a summer concert series, demanding the name of the officer and that he be held accountable. The Wisconsin Chamber Orchestra announced on social media the show was canceled.

News.title: Inflation fall a ‘false dawn’, Burnham warned
News.content:
Falling inflation is a “false dawn” for Andy Burnham, economists warned after the pace of price rises slowed in June.

The consumer prices index (CPI) fell from 2.8pc in May to 2.6pc last month, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS), beating economists’ expectations of a drop to 2.7pc to mark the lowest rate in 15 months.

Lower petrol and diesel prices drove the slowdown amid a short-lived peace deal between the US and Iran, while price pressures from chocolate, oils and fats, dairy and meat also weakened.

However, economists warned a rise in household energy bills in July may already have pushed inflation back up above 3pc.

Suren Thiru, chief economist at the Institute of Chartered Accountants, said: “June’s slowdown is a false dawn as it may have already been reversed this month with higher energy bills, following Ofgem’s energy price cap rise, likely to have lifted inflation above 3pc.”

July’s 13pc increase in the energy price cap has pushed typical annual bills to around £1,862, while renewed fighting between the US and Iran has reignited concerns over oil and gas supplies.

Mr Thiru said elevated inflation would create a fresh headache for John Healey, the newly appointed Chancellor, by squeezing household budgets, raising government borrowing costs and limiting his room for tax cuts or spending increases.

Charlotte O’Leary, at the National Institute of Economic and Social Research, said: “June’s peace deal and the subsequent reduction in oil and gas prices helped cool consumer price inflation. This will be a welcome figure to start the new Prime Minister’s premiership, but the honeymoon period will be short-lived.”

The Bank of England will also be watching closely as it weighs further interest rate cuts, though economists warned renewed instability in the Middle East and higher energy bills could keep inflation close to 3pc for the rest of the year.

Mr Healey said: “Falling inflation is news families want to hear, but there is much more to do to give people the breathing space they need.”

News.title: Russia destroys Ukraine HIV warehouse
News.content:
A Russian missile strike has destroyed $2.6m (£1.9m) worth of HIV prevention supplies in Ukraine, according to an international aid group.

The Alliance for Public Health said the attack on Sunday night near Kyiv hit a warehouse holding 62 million prevention items earmarked for Ukraine’s harm reduction programmes next year. It includes syringes, needles, alcohol wipes, and condoms intended to support more than 300,000 people.

“This is not just another strike. It is an attack on 300,000 Ukrainians who depend on HIV prevention services and on their fundamental right to health,” said Andriy Klepikov, executive director of the Alliance for Public Health.

Efforts to prevent the spread of HIV rely heavily on harm reduction programmes that supply sterile syringes and needles to people who inject drugs, alongside condoms and other supplies that help curb sexual transmission.

Mr Klepikov said the destruction of the warehouse would not immediately disrupt services, because his organisation had moved its supplies for the rest of the year out of central storage and into regional distribution centres several weeks ago as part of contingency planning.

“Russia failed,” he said, adding that the Alliance had notified international partners and appealed for urgent support to rebuild next year’s inventory.

News.title: Private sector pay suffers worst growth since Covid
News.content:
Private sector wages are growing at their slowest pace since the pandemic, piling pressure on Andy Burnham as he enters Downing Street facing a fragile economy and strained public finances.

Salaries rose by 2.9pc in the three months to May, the first time growth has dipped below 3pc since October 2020 and only narrowly ahead of inflation at 2.8pc.

The slowdown was most acute in key industries, with wages in finance and business services up just 2.3pc, manufacturing at 2.5pc and construction earnings falling by 0.2pc over the year.

In contrast, public sector pay accelerated to 5.5pc after striking workers secured higher settlements, widening the gap between state and private sectors.

The cooling labour market came as borrowing overshot official forecasts, leaving John Healey, the new Chancellor, with a £2.7bn gap against expectations.

The Government borrowed £57.6bn between April and June – less than a year earlier but still ahead of projections – pushing public debt to nearly £3tn, or 94.9pc of GDP.

Mr Healey said: “The Prime Minister and I have talked about how we will work in lockstep to meet the fiscal rules with a buffer against uncertainty and how we’ll make life more affordable for working people right across the UK.”

However, Sir Mel Stride, the shadow business secretary, said: “If Andy Burnham and John Healey are really serious about the future of our economy then they must get borrowing under control.”

News.title: Scammers stole $114 billion as Southeast Asia’s crime gangs go corporate
News.content:
Scam gangs stole up to $114 billion from people in Asia-Pacific alone in 2025, the UN has warned, as crime syndicates rapidly professionalise their tactics to evade law enforcement in Southeast Asia.

By way of comparison, the sum dwarfs the $85 billion the UK spends each year on defence.

The Asia-Pacific region has emerged as an epicentre for massive cyber fraud operations since the Covid pandemic. Scammers – some willingly, others under duress – are now stealing billions from internet users across the world via fake romance and cryptocurrency investment schemes.

In 2025, these fraud operations stole between $88.3 and $114.1bn from just people across East Asia, Southeast Asia, Australia and New Zealand, according to a report on Tuesday from the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).

Those figures are triple the estimated losses in 2023, between $18 and $37bn, and don’t account for victims in Europe or the US.

The scam centres – which began in fortified compounds but are now increasingly housed in innocuous office blocks and villas – are found across the region, but have especially exploited power vacuums caused by war, corruption and weak governance in Cambodia, Myanmar and Laos.

Although the scammers initially targeted people in China, they have dramatically expanded their ambitions. The UNODC said people from at least 80 countries and territories had been identified in compounds, with recruiters seeking people from outside Asia as they look to expand new markets.

News.title: UK borrowing costs rise at fastest pace in G7
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs rose at the fastest pace in the G7 after Andy Burnham said he would take a “flexible” approach to the UK’s fiscal rules.

In his maiden speech as prime minister, Mr Burnham on Monday signalled he could bend the rules underpinning Britain’s finances, spooking financial markets fearful of higher government spending.

UK gilts – a benchmark for how much the Government pays on its debt – saw yields rise 0.08 percentage points to an eight-week high of 5.03pc for the 10-year bond. Thirty-year gilts also pushed higher.

The rise was the fastest in the G7, excluding Japan, whose markets are closed for a national holiday.

After markets closed on Monday, Mr Burnham surprised the City by picking John Healey as his next Chancellor.

Mr Healey, who quit over defence funding rising too slowly, will now be tasked with finding billions of pounds in Britain’s stretched public finances.

Shabana Mahmood, the Home Secretary, had widely been expected for the role. Ed Miliband, the former Energy Secretary, was also in contention.

Mr Healey will replace Rachel Reeves, who resigned on Monday.

The appointment of Mr Healey, a veteran of the Blair-Brown government, may calm fears in the City after Mr Burnham pledged to stretch the fiscal rules by using “flexibility” within them.

Speaking in Downing Street, Mr Burnham said: “I’ve said we’ll stick to the fiscal rules, and by that I mean the existing fiscal rules, and use obviously any flexibility within them.”

James Athey, a fund manager at Marlborough, said: “It’s not a good start because bandying around the words fiscal rules seems to be believed within government circles to be a sufficient condition to get financial markets on side, and that just misunderstands an element of the problem.”

He added that investors were watching closely for any signs that the Government will increase borrowing.

Matt Amis, investment director at Aberdeen, said Mr Burnham’s comments had “got the markets’ attention.”

He said “It just shows this week in particular the language from the Burnham administration, the new chancellor, is going to be key here. The gilt market is on edge.”

Mr Burnham, who has become the UK’s seventh prime minister in just a decade, has inherited a troubled economy as businesses grapple with low confidence and strained public finances.

Monday’s comment suggests the new prime minister will use measures to raise borrowing while keeping the additional sums off the Government’s book.

The Resolution Foundation, a think tank, said he could do this by expanding the remit of institutions like the National Wealth Fund, an arms-length government investment vehicle.

His plan to use “flexibility” in the fiscal rules comes after Ms Reeves altered the main indicator of government debt in 2024.

She tweaked the primary measure of the UK’s debt to Public Sector Net Financial Liabilities, meaning that when public financial institutions borrow to invest in a private business it does not count towards the government’s fiscal rules.

However, the think tank warned that boosting the financial capacity of public financial institutions like the National Wealth Fund by £16bn would cost around £400 million a year in debt interest.

Helen Miller, director at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, warned that challenging public finances will mean Mr Burnham will be forced to make tough choices on spending.

She said: “While chancellors come and go, the underlying fiscal constraints remain the same. Public debt, borrowing and debt-interest costs are all high. One in every £12 the government spends currently goes on debt interest.”

Higher borrowing costs threaten to increase the Government’s debt interest bill, which is already forecast to hit £111.2bn for the financial year - equivalent to 8.3pc of public spending.

Mr Burnham said he would announce a set of measures on Tuesday to give households “breathing space” to help with the cost of living.

“I will set out some of those measures starting tomorrow, including how we pay for them,” he said.

“We will help more young people into education... and we will build more council homes. That is the fair and sustainable way to bring the welfare bill down, to meet our fiscal rules and to honour our commitments on defence to our international partners.”

Mr Amis said: “Tomorrow we’re getting some cost of living news. [Burnham] said he was going to state where that funding’s come from. I think that’s key, any unfunded spending from here would get the market’s attention.”

News.title: India approves first dengue vaccine as cases surge in South Asia
News.content:
India has approved its first dengue vaccine as cases of the mosquito-borne disease surge in South Asia.

Japan’s Takeda Pharmaceutical’s dengue vaccine QDENGA has been approved by India’s drug regulator, the Centre Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO).

The global threat posed by dengue has been rising for years, as climate change, urbanisation and international travel aid the spread of the mosquitoes that transmit it.

The approval comes as hospitals across South Asia grapple with a surge in dengue infections.

In Sri Lanka, health authorities reported 2,652 new cases on Sunday alone, taking the total to 76,044 dengue cases so far this year. At least 53 people have died.

Bangladesh is also suffering a major outbreak with over 9,000 cases and 30 deaths that has piled pressure on its health system even as it battles a measles epidemic.

Dengue is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected Aedes mosquitoes.

Its symptoms include fever, severe muscle pain, and in severe cases, shock and internal bleeding that can be fatal.

Although mortality is relatively low, outbreaks place a substantial burden on health systems.

Takeda’s QDENGA jab is a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes. It can be given regardless of previous dengue infections.

“The approval comes at a critical time for public health, as reported dengue cases in India have increased 11-fold in the past two decades,” the company said in a statement.

News.title: Burnham’s plan to restore UK aid spending
News.content:
Andy Burnham is planning to reverse the cuts to Britain’s aid budget made by his predecessors Sir Keir Starmer and Rishi Sunak, according to reports.

A roadmap for returning the UK to spending 0.7 per cent of Gross National Income (GNI) on international aid will be drawn up as part of a major shake-up of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), The Independent reported.

Ed Miliband is set to be named Foreign Secretary and put in charge of overhauling Britain’s international development aims, as well as prioritising climate goals, senior Labour sources said.

The aid spending plan was absent from Mr Burnham’s brief first speech as Prime Minister, in which he pledged to end rough sleeping and bring down the welfare bill in order to fund defence and council housing.

But it follows anger within the Labour Party over what was seen as a broken manifesto promise, when Sir Keir and Rachel Reeves, the Chancellor, slashed aid spending to 0.3 per cent of GNI.

Senior Labour MPs have been lobbying for a return to the 0.7 per cent commitment, a target first established by the United Nations in the 1970s.

It has since become a key yardstick for international efforts to reduce poverty and tackle major health issues like the HIV/AIDS epidemic, vaccine access, and maternal mortality in poor countries.

Sports.title: Wolves star breaks silence on forcing training to be cancelled as he tries to engineer Molineux transfer exit
Sports.content:
WOLVES forward Tolu Arokodare has broken his silence on claims that he forced training to be cancelled after refusing to leave the pitch.

The Nigerian big man is believed to be pushing for a move to Fiorentina, with BBC Sport claiming he demanded the club allow him to move to the Serie A side.



But Wolves instead accepted a more attractive offer from Turkish outfit Trabzonspor.

And on Monday, tensions came to a head when Arokodare reportedly refused to leave the training pitch after being told he was no longer a part of the first-team group.



The refusal prompted new Wolves boss Cesar Peixoto to call time on the session early for the entire team.

And it was claimed that the club had since banned the 25-year-old from the training base entirely, and even hired new security staff to help keep him away.

Arokodare has now broken cover to slam “inaccurate” reporting of the incident in the days since the confrontation.

He wrote in a statement on Instagram: “I was very surprised and disappointed to see the media reports today, many of which are inaccurate.

“Throughout my career, I have always taken great pride in conducting myself professionally and maintaining the highest training standard.

“My commitment has always been to prepare myself as well as possible so that I can contribute to my team-mates and the club whenever I am called upon.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“I remain under contract with Wolves, and my only intention is to fulfil my responsibilities professionally by training, doing my job, and contributing to the team in accordance with that contract.”

It has been a rocky spell at Molineux throughout for Arokodare, who arrived from Genk last summer for more than £23million.

But he has struggled to earn his starting role at the club since, and even clashed with young star Matheus Mane after a heavy loss to West Ham earlier this year.

Now he is expected to leave after the arrival of Adam Armstrong and the return of Raul Jimenez ready for a brutal Championship campaign.

Sports.title: Chelsea quietly complete ‘significant’ transfer for League One wonderkid after he rejected new contract
Sports.content:
CHELSEA have cherrypicked Harrison Bettoni from Wigan after agreeing a four year contract with the League One side.

Bettoni, 18, will spend the season in Chelsea‘s academy on the fringes of Xabi Alonso‘s first team.



The Latics will be owed training compensation for their starlet, who made 27 senior appearances last season.

Wigan reported that Bettoni was offered multiple long-term contracts to remain at the Brick Community Stadium.



But he was ultimately lured towards the Premier League.

Born in Stockport, the forward scored four goals, including his first against Wimbledon to secure Wigan’s goal of the season.

The Wigan academy product came off the bench to score a free-kick equaliser with his first touch.

He then netted a late winner with three minutes remaining, securing Wigan’s first away victory of the campaign.

Bettoni then scored the only goal of the game as Wigan defeated Preston North End in the FA Cup third round.

The youngster also popped up in Arsenal‘s 4-0 victory over the Greater Manchester club in the fourth round of the FA Cup.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Managing Director Sarah Guilfoyle said: “As a Club, we made every possible effort to retain Harrison.

“We offered Harrison multiple strong and competitive long-term offers to remain at Wigan Athletic.

“We are disappointed not to see him continue his journey with us, we respect his decision.

“We’ve worked closely with Chelsea to agree a compensation package that reflects the time, care, and investment our Academy has put into Harrison’s development from a young age.”

Sports.title: ‘Pint of Gaviscon after?’ – Sean Dyche’s explanation of curry order ‘like it’s tactics’ leaves fans in stitches
Sports.content:
FANS were left in stitches after Sean Dyche recounted his curry order.

The experienced Premier League boss, 55, caught up with Jamie Vardy on the ex-England striker’s podcast.



Asked what his ideal takeaway is, Dyche didn’t hold back.

The former Everton, Burnley and Nottingham Forest manager said: “Chilli chicken, mushroom or pilau, I’m not really fussed on that.



“Garlic coriander naan virtually every time. Onion bhaji, saag aloo. I could sing the song but I’m not going to.

“Poppadoms… I even do some sliced red onion. Loads of mango chutney, loads of red onion on.



“Naga’s the biggest one I can do. And I can’t, usually can’t finish it because it hurts that bad. But I do like that pain of a really nasty, harsh curry.

“Then you mix it with just a bit of masala sauce, just a little drizzle, it just softens it a bit. And that is fantastic.”

Vardy laughed before pointing out: “He’s got it down to a tee hasn’t he?”

Dyche then joked: “Years and years of curry abuse.”

Fans adored Dyche’s response.

One wrote on Instagram: “Bros explain it like it was tactics”.

And a second quipped: “Beautiful. Pint of Gaviscon after?”

And another added: “Hes been waiting for someone to ask this for along time”.

Dyche finds himself out of work having been sacked by Forest in February.

The winger is back in England after a difficult three years with Norwich, where he failed to make the grade between 2021 to 2024.



Tzolis has rebuilt his career in Belgium and was on fire last season as Brugge were crowned champions.

He departs Brugge having weighed in with 43 goals and 45 assists in 108 appearances.

Greek businessman Marinakis, 58, owns the two-time European Cup winners and two years ago he gave the green light to set-up a netball franchise.



Hampshire-born ace Pechova, 21, moved over to the East Midlands from Team Bath when they were launched and has flourished, named as Season MVP for 2026.

Though she was not much of a football fan when she arrived, she has loved the close links to the multi-millionaire stars at the City Ground.

Sports.title: Argentina were rotten, violent losers but Liverpool star must now use his misplaced anger
Sports.content:
Argentina were rotten, violent losers but Liverpool star must now use his misplaced anger

Argentina midfielder Alexis Mac Allister claimed other countries have been rejoicing in his country's loss to Spain in the final but Andoni Iraola will be more interested in seeing how it effects his club form

View 2 Images Alexis Mac Allister will return to Liverpool after Argentina's World Cup shenanigans (Image: 2026 Liverpool FC)

Whatever your take on the behaviour of Argentina’s players during and after the World Cup final, you have to admire their siege mentality.

‌



They are getting flak from many angles but are simply doubling down on how proud they are and how the criticism will only make them stronger. There will be no apologies now, or ever. Patriotism is tough to measure but there is clearly no shortage of it amongst Argentinian footballers.

‌



And as a rule, their messages to supporters and their nation tend to be a little more emotional than those put out by English players. Lisandro Martinez even channelled some popular modern philosophy into his reflections on the proceedings.

‌



“Remember that the fall of the great is the joy of the mediocre,” posted Martinez. His Liverpool counterpart, Alexis Mac Allister warmed to the theme, writing: “Thank you to those from other countries who send us messages mocking or rejoicing in our pain. Without meaning to, you help us feel more and more proud to be Argentinian every day.”

Andoni Iraola clarifies future of two Liverpool stars linked with exits READ MORE :

Rodri to Real Madrid transfer truth as Man City contract stipulation revealed READ MORE :

It does not sound as though Mac Allister is up for saying sorry for the conduct of some of his team-mates any time soon. And when he refers to ‘other countries’, you can be sure England is at the top of his list.

It will be intriguing to see what sort of receptions the Premier League’s Argentinian players will get when the new club season starts in the middle of next month. There is unlikely to be open hostility but there will most definitely be reminders of how they behaved in New Jersey on the game’s biggest stage.

‌



When Mac Allister says people were ‘mocking or rejoicing in our pain’, he was mistaken. People were not ‘mocking or rejoicing’, they were simply pointing out that Argentina, on this occasion, proved to be rotten, violent losers.

View 2 Images Alexis Mac Allister was one of Argentina's most influential players in their run to the World Cup final (Image: Juan Luis Diaz/Quality Sport Images/Getty Images)

The same will be pointed out to Mac Allister and Martinez when they take to the field for Liverpool and Manchester United in the Premier League. And Andoni Iraola, in particular, will be hoping the antipathy towards Argentina’s national side proves to be a spur for Mac Allister after what was pretty much a season-long trough in form.

‌



In 37 Premier League appearances for Liverpool last season, Mac Allister contributed two goals and four assists. In 35 appearances in the 2024/25 campaign, he contributed five goals and five assists.

He was tireless in the World Cup - only Rodri covered more distance in the tournament - but often looked off the pace as Liverpool laboured to their fifth-placed finish. After reports linking Mac Allister with a move to Real Madrid, Iraola was compelled to stress that he wanted to keep the 27-year-old.

The new Liverpool manager said: “I think Alexis has been one of the best players at the club for the last few years, and he has had a very good World Cup, so it is normal that other clubs want our best players. But I want to keep my good players.”

‌



Fair enough. But there is surely no doubt he wants to keep the Mac Allister of 24/25 rather than the Mac Allister of 25/26.

Perhaps his anger at the ‘mocking and rejoicing’ will inspire him to get back to his best. Liverpool fans and Iraola will certainly hope so.

Sports.title: Furious Argentina fans launch petition to replay 'corrupt' Spain World Cup final
Sports.content:
Furious Argentina fans launch petition to replay 'corrupt' Spain World Cup final

Argentina were denied back-to-back World Cup titles when Spain beat them 1-0 in the final in New Jersey and their furious supporters are not taking the loss well

View 2 Images Spain lifted the World Cup on Sunday (Image: Getty Images)

Thousands of angry Argentina fans are demanding that the World Cup final be replayed due to a "corrupt" referee.

‌



Argentina were beaten 1-0 by Spain in extra time of the showpiece finale in New Jersey on Sunday. Ferran Torres' goal settled it for the dominant Spanish side, who bombarded the Argentina goal throughout the match.

‌



Defending champions Argentina failed to muster a single shot on target over the 120 minutes and were down to 10 men following Enzo Fernandez's red card in the 93rd minute. Goalkeeper Emi Martinez was extremely busy before finally being beaten by Torres' effort in the 106th minute.

‌



Argentina did not take the defeat well, with ugly scenes following the full-time whistle. Leandro Paredes was spotted kicking and punching as he shoved Eric Garcia to the ground and grappled with Gavi, while Nauel Molina appeared to have instigated the altercation by throwing a punch at Rodri.

Norway to make formal Donald Trump complaint over 'serious' breach of World Cup rules READ MORE :

Mirror readers crown World Cup's best pundit as Wayne Rooney beats Roy Keane READ MORE :

Some fans of the team are similarly bitter, judging by the more than 82,000 signatures on a petition calling for the final to be replayed. The Change.org petition's author Gisela Sanchez argues that FIFA should scrub the result due to the performance of Slovenian referee Slavko Vincic.

“The recent final between Argentina and Spain was tarnished by the controversial and corrupt performance of the referee who, according to video evidence, was bought to influence the match’s outcome," Sanchez writes.

‌



“It is a monumental disappointment for the players, coaches, and, above all, for the fans who crave to see a game decided by talent and dedication on the pitch, and not by rigged refereeing decisions.

“If we allow corruption to go unnoticed on this global stage, we are setting a bad example for future generations of athletes and fans.

View 2 Images Slavko Vincic was busy in the World Cup final (Image: Buda Mendes, Getty Images)

‌



“Therefore, we ask Fifa to review these incidents with seriousness and transparency, and to consider replaying the final – this time without the influence of a corrupt referee.”

Change.org is flooded with petitions of a very different nature - ones which call for FIFA to ban Argentina from future tournaments. One calling for the team to be banned from ALL future World Cups racked up over 29 million signatures before closing.

Vincic blew his whistle on 46 occasions for fouls, 25 of which were committed by Argentina players. Fernandez was sent off after picking up two yellow cards in the second half - one for dissent having not been awarded a free-kick and one for a reckless challenge on Pau Cubarsi.

‌



The match was played in a stop-start nature due to Argentina's spoiling tactics, but Spain eventually found a way through in extra time. FIFA are investigating the behaviour of Argentina's players in the aftermath of the match, which was widely slammed.

"It's a disgrace," Gary Neville said on ITV. “I love the competitiveness of the Argentines, fighting and scrapping for their lives, Messi has propped them up, but it’s been a disgrace the last few games."

Sports.title: World Cup-related violence rocketed at home but England football fans 'impeccable' in US
Sports.content:
World Cup-related violence rocketed at home but England football fans 'impeccable' in US

The tournament saw highest number of football-related arrests in the UK since Euro 2020. There was a shocking rise in incidents of domestic violence, disorder and online hate, police said today

Fans across the UK go wild as England open score against Argentina

England fans were 'impeccably behaved' at the World Cup in the US, police chiefs said today.

‌



But it was a very different picture at home, with the highest number of football-related arrests in the UK since Euro 2020. The World Cup saw a shocking rise in incidents of domestic violence, disorder and online hate.

‌



Mark Roberts, the head of UK Football Policing, warned that alcohol and the relaxation of licensing laws in England, announced with only 48 hours' notice, contributed to the disturbing rise in violence.

‌



View 3 Images Police respond to trouble in Bournemouth after England's World Cup defeat to Argentina (Image: Max Willcock/BNPS)

Not checking one body part 'regularly' increases risk of dementia by 500 per cent READ MORE :

Cheshire Police Chief Constable Mr Roberts said: "The fans' behaviour at the World Cup was really good again. We have to get rid of the outdated image of our fans based on historical behaviour.

"We asked police to judge our fans on their actions and not any preconceptions and police in the US and Mexico did that. Our fans got into the spirit of it, both England and Scotland fans were there to have a really good time.

‌



View 3 Images UK head of football policing unit Mark Roberts (Image: Cheshire Police)

"They behaved brilliantly and had a really good impact on the economies in the US and Mexico. England fans knew how to party, too. Arrests were at a really low level."

There were only 22 arrests at the England World Cup games abroad in total, including ticket touting. But Mr Roberts added: "This was the worst tournament we have seen domestically for some time, the worst since Euro 2020.

‌



"That is a real concern for us as we are hosting the tournament in 2028. Domestic abuse was a real factor. It is not just about football. Alcohol and drugs play a big role. So it is a societal issue, not a footballing one.

"But unfortunately, this has really negative consequences. Online abuse, typically of a racist nature, also increased again. There was a rise in incidents at licensed premises. A significant number were reported to police; there was an additional round so England played an extra game, which needs to be factored in.

"It is the best result in 60 years since winning it, so we saw these problems, even when the team was comparatively successful. So it was a more depressing picture back in the UK.

‌



View 3 Images England fans at a World Cup party in America (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

"We saw the highest number of reported incidents of domestic abuse around tournaments, and there were allegations of spiking in licenced premises. That is something we will examine regarding violence against women and girls. We are looking to learn from this."

A total of 2,322 incidents were reported to the police, with 391 arrests, the number of incidents rose at pubs and bars as the tournament progressed.

‌



There were 1487 incidents linked to the Russia 2018 World Cup, with 337 arrests; 573 linked to the 2022 tournament in Qatar, and 1302 at Euro 2024, with 321 arrests.

At the delayed Euro 2020 tournament, held in the summer of 2021, there were 2,345 incidents, and 599 arrests, with shocking scenes of violence before the final at Wembley as large numbers of fans tried to get in without tickets.

"We want to make the point that the extension of licensing laws needs to take the consequences of relaxation into account," added Mr Roberts.

‌



"Please take into account the negative impact as well as the positive. We need to make decisions well in advance so we can implement measures."

There were stabbings and police stations were attacked as well as the rise in domestic violence, and violence between the fans of Morocco and France in London.

In the US, by contrast, England fans helped make their games a "memorable experience” for the host cities. Mr Roberts praised the work of the FA and the Football Supporters Association in keeping fans informed while travelling abroad.

Article continues below

It was estimated that around 10,000 to 13,000 fans travelled from the UK to our group games in the US, with a huge number also travelling to Mexico for the round of 32 game at the famous Azteca stadium.

There were around 2,500 official fan club members at the Argentina game, but the numbers were boosted by ex-pat and US fans wearing the team colours.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford will have to confront awkward Man Utd reality when he returns to Old Trafford
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford will have to confront awkward Man Utd reality when he returns to Old Trafford

Marcus Rashford is set to be part of Manchester United training this summer but a notable decision was made in his time away from Old Trafford

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford has twice been loaned out by Manchester United (Image: DeFodi Images, DeFodi Images via Getty Images)

Marcus Rashford faces an uncomfortable situation upon his return to Manchester United, as he currently finds himself without a squad number. His last outing for United came in December 2024, before spells away on loan at Aston Villa and Barcelona.

‌



The 28-year-old displayed glimpses of top form at Villa before moving to Barcelona on loan last summer. Rashford contributed 14 goals and 14 assists across all competitions as the Catalan giants clinched La Liga, though Barcelona chose not to activate their £26million purchase option. A further £40m release clause has also now lapsed for other interested clubs.

‌



Rashford is due to rejoin United training following his summer break. The England international featured in the squad that secured World Cup bronze, making six appearances, including three starts.

‌



Despite being sidelined under former boss Ruben Amorim, Rashford's representatives have had encouraging discussions with United about his pre-season return. However, the forward must navigate a potentially uncomfortable situation as he looks to select a new United squad number, having lost the iconic number 10 shirt while away from Old Trafford.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The iconic number 10 was handed to Matheus Cunha following his switch from Wolves last year. It had belonged to Rashford since 2018, following in the footsteps of many United legends, including Wayne Rooney.

‌



Michael Carrick axes five Man Utd stars as major rebuild gathers pace READ MORE :

Alex Scott transfer twist as Bournemouth star ‘keen’ on rivals amid Arsenal and Man Utd race READ MORE :

Rashford originally wore number 39 when he made his breakthrough during the 2015/16 season. He then took the number 19 shirt for the following two campaigns before receiving the prestigious number 10.

In 2018, Rashford tweeted about his new number: "Wearing the shirt worn by United legends, honoured." United boss Jose Mourinho explained the reason for giving the then-20-year-old the iconic number.

"He wanted it," Mourinho told MUTV in 2018. "He always wanted it. Of course, he respected the big Rooney and then Zlatan wanted to have it.

‌



View 2 Images Rashford previously wore the number 10 shirt for Manchester Unted (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

"Of course, he was in the shadow, waiting for the opportunity and now the shirt is empty. It's something fantastic for the kid, let's give the shirt to him".

During his spell away from Old Trafford, Rashford wore nine for Villa, a number he'd previously donned for United's academy teams. He also took the number 14 shirt throughout his season with Barcelona.

‌



Both numbers from his respective loan stints are currently available at United. Beyond nine and 14, numbers 20, 21 and 24 are also free for Rashford within the top 25 squad positions.

However, when it comes to his other former United squad numbers, Bryan Mbeumo currently wears 19 and youngster Tyler Fletcher has 39 in Michael Carrick's side. Summer arrivals Andrey Santos and Youri Tieleman have been handed 17 and 18, respectively, while new backup goalkeeper Karl Darlow will sport number 12.

Sports.content:
Mirror readers crown World Cup's best pundit as Wayne Rooney beats Roy Keane

The World Cup is over and while Spain beat Argentina in the final to take home the trophy, there was a different battle being waged on our screens between the BBC and ITV

View 2 Images Wayne Rooney has been a hit on the BBC this summer (Image: BBC)

Wayne Rooney has been crowned as the best pundit during the World Cup by Mirror readers. The former England and Manchester United striker was one of the BBC's star signings for the tournament and made an impact with viewers.

‌



The 40-year-old has taken to punditry in recent years after his foray into management ended with Plymouth Argyle in 2024. While he largely struggled in the dugout, Rooney has settled well in front of the camera, with his analysis and standing in the game a good combination.

‌



He was a regular fixture on the BBC during the 104-game World Cup in North America, providing some memorable moments. His brutally honest opinion on the World Cup final half-time show, which featured Madonna, the Muppets, Justin Bieber and Shakira, went viral and appears to have gone down well with viewers.

‌



The Mirror asked readers to vote for their favourite World Cup pundit, with Rooney up against his ex-Manchester United team-mates Gary Neville and Roy Keane, as well as their ITV colleague Emma Hayes.

All 37 World Cup pundits ranked as BBC vs ITV winner decided and unexpected star emerges READ MORE :

We received 4,604 votes, with Rooney coming out as the clear winner, attracting Rooney 41 per cent of the clicks ahead of Keane on 29 per cent. Former Chelsea women boss Hayes got 7 per cent, while came in last on Neville 6 per cent, with 16 per cent voting for other.

Rooney, who reportedly signed a two-year contract with the BBC in 2025 which is worth £800,000, was given plenty of responsibility to conduct the tactical analysis around games. His forthright opinions, particularly on Thomas Tuchel's approach with England, won over audiences.

‌



Meanwhile, his comfort on screen with former England team-mates Joe Hart and Micah Richards shone through. And the fact he followed through with his promise to go rowing after Norway made it to the quarter-finals and he lost a bet with Erling Halaand showed his lighter side.

View 2 Images The results of the Mirror's best World Cup pundit poll (Image: Mirror)

Agree with the outcome? Have your say in the comments section below.

‌



ITV's coverage saw Keane, Neville and Ian Wright take centre stage as their top pundits, while Hayes was used to give in-depth tactical analysis during the hydration breaks. Keane was on his typical form, but clearly Neville's opinions didn't go down as well.

Rooney's win reflects wider viewing habits, with the BBC comfortably beating ITV in the ratings battle for the final between Spain and Argentina. With both channels showing the showpiece on Sunday in New Jersey, the BBC's average audience of 9.7 million viewers was far higher than ITV's 2.4m. The BBC peaked at 13.6m, ahead of ITV's 3.4m.

BBC bosses will likely see the figures as vindication for their decision not to broadcast the majority of the tournament from the United States. While ITV forked out for an impressive Brooklyn studio, the BBC anchored the vast majority of their coverage from Salford.

Sports.title: Rodri to Real Madrid transfer truth as Man City contract stipulation revealed
Sports.content:
Rodri to Real Madrid transfer truth as Man City contract stipulation revealed

The Spain captain is on a high after winning the World Cup and being named player of the tournament, but his club future has been in question for some time

View 2 Images Rodri of Manchester City (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

Manchester City bosses will resist all attempts from Real Madrid to sign Rodri this summer.

‌



Spanish giants Real have made the World Cup winner one of their No.1 priorities. Rodri has entered the final 12 months of his current deal and has not agreed a new one at the Etihad.

‌



The midfielder's stock has never been higher, following his sensational exploits with Spain in North America this summer and one particular high-profile social media account has gone into overdrive in recent days.

‌



Real president Florentino Perez is said to be preparing an initial £80m bid - and is even prepared to go to £100m for someone who will be available on a free transfer in 12 months time. But City chairman Khaldoon Al-Mubarak is set to hold firm - and rebuff his rivals from the Spanish capital.

Norway to make formal Donald Trump complaint over 'serious' breach of World Cup rules READ MORE :

Pep Guardiola names his price after job rejection as England possibility opens up READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

New boss Enzo Maresca has made it clear he wants to keep Rodri at all costs.

‌



Maresca, who will speak to the media for the first time on Friday since replacing Pep Guardiola, made this stipulation when negotiating his deal to become the new manager six months ago.

The Italian is planning to build his team around Rodri, and views the defensive midfielder as crucial when it comes to integrating new £116m signing Elliot Anderson into the side.

View 2 Images Rodri helped Spain to the World Cup this summer (Image: Getty Images)

‌



City bosses are still hopeful of agreeing a new deal with Rodri that would secure his long-term future. But despite all his success in Manchester, the 30-year-old still harbours long-held ambitions to play for Real before he retires.

Which means he could decide to run down his contract and leave the Etihad for nothing next summer.

Rodri joined City from Atletico Madrid in 2019 for £62.6m and has gone on to become one of the most decorated players in the club's history.

‌



Rodri has won 13 major trophies, including the Treble in 2023, as well as winning the Ballon d'Or in 2024, at the expense of Real's Vinicius Junior.

He is also favourite to land the individual honour again next time round.

Sports.title: Man City had more fans arrested than any other club in 2025-26 as top five revealed
Sports.content:
Man City had more fans arrested than any other club in 2025-26 as top five revealed

Data has been released surrounding football-related arrests during the 2025-26 season and Manchester City fans topped the table ahead of Chelsea

View 2 Images There were 1,963 football related arrests last season (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester City supporters were arrested the most out of all football fans last season, new police figures have revealed. The UK Government released data looking at the 2025/26 campaign.

‌



The data, which accounts for data collected by the 43 territorial police forces in England and Wales, and by the British Transport Police (BTP), has taken a close look at the amount of football-related arrests and action taken by the authorities over the past 12 months.

‌



In all, it has confirmed that there were 1,963 football-related arrests and other police actions across the country. This is actually a decrease of 4% compared to last season.

‌



This is a noteworthy figure given the change in legislation midway through the season. In March, it was confirmed that unauthorised entry to a football stadium was added to Schedule 1 of the Football Spectators Act 1989. In all, 45 arrests and police actions were made for offences of that nature.

Norway to make formal Donald Trump complaint over 'serious' breach of World Cup rules READ MORE :

When it comes to specific clubs, the Government have confirmed that Man City had the most arrests, closely followed by Premier League rivals Chelsea and Manchester United.

The data read: “The club with the highest number of supporters arrested or subject to other police actions in the 2025 to 2026 domestic football season was Manchester City, with 102 arrests and other police actions. Chelsea was second, with 76, and Manchester United third, with 67.”

‌



Other clubs to feature in the top five include Premier League champions Arsenal, who had 66 arrests, while Championship side Millwall are slightly behind with 63.

View 2 Images Man City fans had the most arrests last season according to Government data (Image: Getty Images)

The data added: “In the 2025 to 2026 domestic football season, Manchester United had the largest decrease in the number of supporters arrested or subject to other police actions compared with the 2024 to 2025 season (-60; -47%). This follows a large increase in the number of arrests and other police actions in the 2024 to 2025 season (+39; +44% compared with the 2023 to 2024 season).”

‌



“Portsmouth had the largest increase in arrests and other police actions compared with the 2024 to 2025 season (from 16 to 55 arrests and other police actions).”

A number of high-profile Premier League clubs also feature in the list of the highest amount of football banning orders. West Ham remain at the top of the list with 121, compared to 112 last season. Chelsea, Manchester United, Manchester City and Liverpool also rank in the top five, with each of those clubs having supporters in the 80s with football banning orders.

Sports.title: Johnson-Thompson and Asher-Smith out of Commonwealth Games
Sports.content:
Commonwealth Games 2026: Katarina Johnson-Thompson, Dina Asher-Smith and netball star Natalie Metcalf out of Glasgow 2026

Katarina Johnson-Thompson is out of the Commonwealth Games

England medal hopes Katarina Johnson-Thompson and Dina Asher-Smith have pulled out of the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

Johnson-Thompson was one of the favourites for the heptathlon, having won gold at the Gold Coast in 2018 and Birmingham 2022, while Asher-Smith was set to compete in the relays.

Fellow Olympic medallists Matthew Hudson-Smith and Daryll Neita have also announced their withdrawals alongside Amber Anning, Zac Sneddon, Anna Purchase, Elliot Giles and Jona Efoloko on the day of the opening ceremony, which takes place on Thursday night.

The reason for Johnson-Thompson and Asher-Smith's withdrawals have not been stated, although it is presumed they are prioritising next month's European Championships in Birmingham.

The hectic schedule has presented a quandary for a number of leading athletes, including Olympic champion Keely Hodgkinson, who decided not to pursue selection for the Glasgow Games.

Dina Asher-Smith is one of nine England athletics members to pull out on the eve of Glasgow 2026

International stars who have previously pulled out of the Games include multiple Olympic swimming medallists Kaylee McKeown and Summer McIntosh of Australia and Canada respectively, and Hodgkinson's 800m rival, Mary Moraa of Kenya.

Also on Thursday, England netball star Natalie Metcalf withdrew from the Games because of a calf injury.

Metcalf, who was part of the 2018 squad that won Commonwealth gold in Australia, has been replaced by Ella Clark.

Sports.title: Arsenal complete deal to sign winger Tzolis
Sports.content:
Arsenal have announced the signing of winger Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge on a five-year deal.

The fee is understood to be £34m, which is a record for the Belgian Pro League.

The 24-year-old, formerly of Norwich City, scored 17 goals and provided 23 assists in 36 league appearances last season.

Sky Sports News understands that Morgan Rogers was identified as the club's top attacking target, but the England international instead completed a British-record £117m move to London rivals Chelsea.

Tzolis has been signed as a replacement for Leandro Trossard, who departed for Besiktas in a £17m deal

Image: Tzolis played against Arsenal in the Champions League last season

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz:

Tzolis arrives as Trossard's direct replacement. And a closer look at Tzolis' profile shows a lot of similarities between the two players.

The first is the profile. Through those who know him, the Greek forward is a winger but like Trossard, he is also a No 10. Last summer, Crystal Palace strongly considered Tzolis as a replacement for now-Arsenal star Eberechi Eze.

Image: Tzolis is predominantly a left winger but can also play as a No 10

"He's able to fulfil different roles," Hayk Milkon tells Sky Sports, who was Club Brugge's assistant manager for Tzolis' entire time in Belgium up until February of this year.

"Coming from the left side - giving him this space to start wide and then find the moments to get more inside - that's where he's at his strongest.

"If he's assigned to play really wide to get these one on ones, he's able to do it. But he's always strongest the closer he is to the goal. Whenever he's more central, you can expect him at any moment to attack the space."

Another similarity between Tzolis and Trossard is their availability. Trossard had an exemplary injury record at Arsenal and was only injured for four matches in three-and-a-half years. All of those four games came in his final season in north London.

"He's a guy that works a lot," adds Milkon. "He runs a lot of kilometres in the game, but also at high speeds and his sprint distance.

Sports.title: Rowley steps down as St Helens head coach
Sports.content:
Paul Rowley has stepped down as St Helens coach with immediate effect.

Saints have endured a difficult season by their high standards as they currently hold the final play-off position in sixth place by two points - ahead of Hull KR who have a game in hand - having never missed the Super League play-offs.

Assistant coach Eamon O'Carroll will assume interim leadership of the team ahead of their Rivals Round match against Wigan Warriors on Friday, live on Sky Sports at 8pm (build-up from 7.30pm).

"I would like to thank Paul for his commitment and extreme hard work as our head coach. He will always be warmly welcomed at the club," said St Helens chairman Eamonn McManus.

"The decision was an extremely difficult one for all concerned, and we fully recognise the extra challenges that Paul faced with us this particular season.

"We as a club must now look forward and do all within our powers to preserve our position as the most successful club in the history of Super League and to restore our position as a silverware contender going forward."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League match between St Helens and Toulouse earlier this month

Rowley became Saints head coach at the end of last year after a troubled season with Salford Red Devils, where financial issues led them to finish bottom of the Super League.

Saints are six points behind league leaders Leeds Rhinos but suffered a 46-0 hammering to Toulouse earlier this month - the first time they had been held scoreless at home since 1980.

They were also thrashed 32-0 by Wigan Warriors in the semi-finals of the Challenge Cup.

Sky Sports News has previously reported United's long-term interest in Baleba, and despite his struggle for form last season, he remains of interest to Michael Carrick's side.

It is understood the club have made movement in revisiting a potential deal for the 22-year-old this summer, but no official club-to-club contact has been made yet, and a compromise around the player's valuation would need to be found.

Marco Rose's side do not want to sell the talented midfielder, who has entered the final two years of his current contract, and have already knocked back inquiries from the Premier League trio.

Singh on set at Sky Sports News

The second half of the World Cup coincided with the start of South Asian Heritage Month in the UK - and it was great to celebrate with two trailblazers on set at Sky Sports News.

Our resident transfers guru Dharmesh Sheth has been a regular fixture on Sky Sports News for more than 20 years and someone who's helped pave the way for under-represented communities in sports media. He was joined on set by New Zealand international footballer Sarpreet Singh.

Singh idolised Didier Drogba growing up and would wake up in the middle of the night in New Zealand to watch the Premier League great in action for Chelsea.

While he never got to play against Drogba, Singh did play against England in New Zealand's pre-World Cup friendly with the Three Lions in Tampa.

"It was such an amazing experience to be up against the likes of Harry Kane and Marcus Rashford who I watched play [for ages] in the Premier League. It was another dream come true moment, but I was just trying to do the best job for my country."

Had things worked out differently, Singh could have been lining up alongside Kane at club level next season. Singh spent four seasons with Bayern Munich after the Bavarian giants signed him following his impressive showing for New Zealand at the 2019 FIFA U20 World Cup.

"It was such an unreal experience," said Singh, who played against Tottenham in the 2019 Audi Cup final before making his Bundesliga debut later that year.

Image: Sarpreet Singh made his Bundesliga debut for Bayern Munich in 2019 when he replaced Philippe Coutinho in a 6-1 win over Werder Bremen

"It was amazing to be around one of the biggest clubs in the world and to learn from some of the best on a daily basis.

"Hansi Flick (the current Barcelona manager) was in charge. Alphonso Davies and Joshua Zirkzee were there at the time, so we are all mates."

An investment consortium led by British-Indian millionaire and former QPR co-owner Amit Bhatia has expressed an interest in acquiring a minority stake in Liverpool.

Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG) acknowledged the approach on the same day that Bhatia stepped down from the board at QPR to end an 18-year association, having agreed to transfer his stake in the club to majority owner Ruben Gnanalingam.

Image: Amit Bhatia was QPR's co-owner until July 21, when he transferred his share of the club to Ruben Gnanalingam.

A spokesperson for FSG said: "An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club."

Sky News has since revealed that Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has also been approached to join the consortium.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky News' Mark Kleinman discusses Amazon founder Jeff Bezos' potential involvement in a consortium, led by former QPR co-owner Amit Bhatia, to buy a stake in Liverpool.

No deal has been agreed with discussions at an early stage. FSG bought Liverpool in 2010 for £300m. Forbes recently valued the club at £4.6bn.

On Tuesday, Bhatia announced he was leaving his role at QPR, saying the club "has been a deeply important part of my life and of my family's life". He served as vice-chairman before becoming chairman in 2018, a role he held for five years.

Image: Will Amit Bhatia succeed in his attempt to acquire a strategic minority stake in Liverpool Football Club?

Bhatia is the son-in-law of Lakshimi Mittal, who is the executive of steel and mining company ArcelorMittal.

Mittal is worth an estimated £23.2bn.

The forward scored a breathtaking goal, chipped in with an assist and even missed a penalty in the game as Singh Sabha Slough ran out 2-0 winners - although they forfeited the trophy as Antonio had not been officially registered to play beforehand.

Image: Michail Antonio joins the Singh Sabha Slough boys for a photo

Danny Barham, who was a Singh Sabha Slough guest player alongside Antonio, told Sky Sports News: "He joined the team through one of our players as their children go to school together and had to leave at 7am from London to get there for a 10am kick-off.

"He was the nicest person you could ever meet, probably the nicest person I've ever met!

Image: Michail Antonio (bottom right) and Danny Barham (third from bottom right) with their Singh Sabha Slough team-mates at the KFF tournament Leicester

"The team we were playing weren't originally going to let him play, so Singh Sabha Slough disqualified themselves just to let him play in the game.

"He scored an absolute worldie from outside the box with no backlift - almost like Ronaldinho's goal against Chelsea in the Champions League - and he also assisted for the second goal.

"Technically, you see why he is a pro compared to everyone else [and] there was no attitude, he played as if it was his own team. But you could see the difference playing with a pro."

Image: Jarnail Singh flanked by sons Bhupinder Singh Gill (R) and Sunny Singh Gill (L)

The match was refereed by Jarnail Singh, who is the father of trailblazing match officials Sunny Singh Gill and Bhupinder Singh Gill.

Singh, who remains the only turbaned Sikh ever to have refereed in the English Football League, told Sky Sports News: "I used to play in KFF tournaments in the early 80s and have been refereeing at them for many, many years.

Image: Michail Antonio and an opposition player are tracked by referee Jarnail Singh at the KFF tournament Leicester

"Michail was a really nice, humble bloke and he was playing for the fun of it with a big smile on his face.

"The people watching enjoyed seeing him and more came over to watch when they realised he was playing. He was nice and he stayed behind to take photos with everyone."

For more stories, features and videos, visit our ground-breaking South Asians in football page on skysports.com and stay tuned to Sky Sports News and our Sky Sports digital platforms.

Miami Heat have confirmed a video teasing LeBron James' potential return to the NBA franchise was posted by mistake.

A live stream titled "LeBron James Introductory Press Conference", scheduled for July 27, was uploaded to the Heat's YouTube channel on Tuesday night but was later deleted.

A Miami Heat spokesperson later confirmed the video was mistakenly posted in preparation for James potentially returning to the team with which he won two championships.

The error has sent the basketball world into a frenzy as it awaits confirmation of where James will play his 24th NBA season.

James' next step has dominated the news agenda ever since the 41-year-old confirmed he would be leaving the Los Angeles Lakers after eight seasons in June.

The Cleveland Cavaliers, Philadelphia 76ers and Miami Heat have all been linked with the four-time NBA MVP.
