Sports.title: Commonwealth Games stars issued STI warning by sexual health clinic after surge in patients at previous event - as expert tells athletes to bring their OWN condoms following shortage at the Winter Olympics
Sports.content:
Commonwealth Games stars have been sent a warning by a sexual health expert ahead of the event getting underway on Thursday.

The action is set to take place in Glasgow from July 23 to August 2, but as the Games return to the Scottish city for the first time since 2014, athletes, visitors and local communities have been urged to make sexual wellbeing part of their plans.

One sexual health nurse, speaking anonymously, revealed their clinic saw an increase in STI diagnoses and demand for sexual health services in the aftermath of the event 12 years ago.

And, this time, experts have told athletes to carry contraception with them and undergo tests if they have unprotected sex or a new sexual partner.

Sarah Mulindwa, a Senior Sexual Health Nurse and TV presenter said: 'Planning ahead for your sexual health is no different from preparing for a heatwave – carry condoms if you think you may need them, know where to access healthcare and look out for your friends.

'The Commonwealth Games are an exciting opportunity for people from around the world to come together and celebrate sport, but we want everyone to enjoy the event while looking after their health.

A sexual health expert has sent a warning to Commonwealth Games stars ahead of the event

'Carry condoms if you think you may need them, get tested if you've had unprotected sex or a new sexual partner, and seek advice promptly if you're worried about HIV exposure or need emergency contraception. Looking after your sexual health is a normal part of looking after your overall wellbeing.'

Condoms are usually widely available for athletes at major sporting events, although there was drama during the Winter Olympics earlier this year when the athletes village reportedly ran out of condoms.

That came after organisers slashed the usual supply from 300,000 to a mere 10,000.

At the time, an anonymous athlete told Italian newspaper La Stampa: 'The supplies sold out in just three days. They promised us more will arrive but who knows when.'

Discussing that incident, the organising committee said: 'We can confirm that condom supplies in the Olympic villages were temporarily depleted due to higher-than-anticipated demand.'

Additional supplies were subsequently delivered and distributed to alleviate the issue.

Sports.title: Shocking moment England youth stars scrap in wild hotel brawl as team-mates stand around laughing and recording on their phones instead of breaking up fight
Sports.content:
Shocking footage has emerged of two England youth players brawling during an international camp - while their team-mates egg them on and stand around filming.

The video features two youngsters from a youth team.

Daily Mail Sport understands that the scrap began after one of the players was teased for having a Nokia mobile phone.

One of them appears to be the aggressor in the footage, being encouraged by team-mates to 'f*** him up' as he grabs the other and pushes him onto a hotel bed with his hand around his neck.

The youth holds his team-mate in that position for a couple of seconds as others get in closer to film him in the vulnerable position.

He then starts punching his team-mate but the other then kicks him off the bed and the pair continue fighting.

Two England youth players are seen in a shocking hotel-room fight caught on camera

The scrap began after one of the players was teased for having a Nokia mobile phone

The fight spills onto the floor, with one holding the other against the wall and putting him in a headlock. A player is heard screaming, but it is unclear who.

At that point, the initiator lets up before being told to 'carry on, man'. He then shoves the other boy onto the bed and is again told to 'f*** him up'.

In the background, team-mates are told to 'shut the door' multiple times. They then get out of the way and laugh as the brawl continues.

Throughout the scene, the players remain dressed in their England kits.

The episode raises concerns about the safeguarding of youngsters on England duty.

Daily Mail Sport was told by the FA: 'We were made aware of an internal matter during an MU16s camp in October 2025.

'This was quickly resolved at the time.'

Daily Mail Sport has also contacted the clubs of the respective players for comment.

Mobile phones are seen as divisive, distracting and a risk to mental health by both schools and football teams.

Some football managers - including Pep Guardiola and Erik ten Hag when they were in Manchester - have banned them to improve their players' focus.

Sports.title: The greatest glow ups in football history after Real Madrid and Brazil star Vinicius Jr undergoes chin surgery
Sports.content:
Vinicius Junior surprised fans this week as the Brazilian star revealed the cosmetic work he 's undergone to enhance his jawline.

The Real Madrid winger had a popular new ‘chin harmonisation’ procedure in recent weeks and revealed his transformation on Instagram.

The reaction has been mixed, with many fans left shocked.

But the star has also received support and admiration from non–football fans and supporters alike.

In light of Vinicius Junior’s transformation and the bold step the former Champions League winner has taken, the Daily Mail has examined some of the more famous and dramatic cosmetic changes made by footballers.

Brazil superstar Vinicius Jr looks a completely different man (right) after undergoing chin harmonisation surgery

Cristiano Ronaldo

As one of the most followed and photographed men on the planet, Cristiano Ronaldo has understandably always valued his appearance and looking good.

Speculation has been rife over the years that the five-time Ballon d'Or winner has undergone a number of cosmetic interventions.

The 41-year-old has never publicly confirmed it, but his image carries a number of distinct differences to his teenage years.

The most notable appears to have been work Ronaldo has had done on his teeth.

After joining Man United as a young talent from Sporting Lisbon, Ronaldo at some stage in late 2003, early 2004 was seen with a brand-new glistening set of veneers.

Ronaldo's teeth are not the only part of his appearance fans have speculated that he has had amended surgically throughout his magnificent career. The all-time Champions League top goal scorer in part due to his relentless training regime and passion for physical fitness even away from football, is a completely different specimen to the shy, skinny Madeiran who Sir Alex Ferguson brought to Old Trafford all those years ago.

However, there has always been discussion that he also owes part of his chiselled appearance to various cosmetic facial procedures.

Again, whilst Ronaldo has never confirmed it, fans have often suspected that the Portuguese icon has potentially had some sort of botox and thermage treatments to strengthen his jawline and define his cheek bones as well as having a small degree of rhinoplasty work completed to reshape his nose.

Speculation has long been rife that Cristiano Ronaldo has undergone cosmetic work over the years

Jurgen Klopp and Roberto Firmino

Former Liverpool manager Jurgen Klopp and forward Roberto Firmino were well-known for the dental work they had done during their time at Anfield.

Whilst people naturally change in appearance over time, the abrupt nature of Klopp and Firmino’s abrupt ‘glow ups’ revealed the extent of the work undertaken.

In his early years as a manager in Germany at Mainz and eventually Borussia Dortmund, Klopp had a much less polished look with school-boy curtains and slightly discoloured teeth.

By the time he arrived at Anfield he had already completely transformed into a different man identifiable mainly by his glimmering set of veneers.

One wonders whether that may have inspired his future Champions League winning forward Firmino to get his own work done.

As just months after joining Liverpool in the summer of 2015 the Brazilian must have asked his new boss for some recommendations as by the following season he had a new set of whites.

Former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp famously underwent dental work during his time at Anfield

Former Liverpool forward Roberto Firmino also notably had work done on his teeth

Rob Holding and Gabriel

Perhaps the most common cosmetic procedure amongst modern footballers alongside extreme dental work is a hair transplant.

Two prime examples of Premier League footballers receiving hair transplants are former Arsenal centre half Rob Holding and his ex-teammate Gabriel Magalhaes.

The two defenders underwent near full transplants and both enjoyed great success with their procedures.

Both players have been relatively open and honest about their new set of locks, with Gabriel in particular actually helping advertise the clinic that restored his hairline, then again unlike botox and other facial augmentation a hair transplant is immediately apparent.

Rob Holding underwent a hair transplant in 2021 that saw his previously receding hair (left - pictured early 2021), transformed into a healthy mop of hair (right - pictured in 2023)

Arsenal defender Gabriel has promoted the clinic where he underwent his transplant

Wayne Rooney

One of the first players to publicly announce they had undergone a hair transplant five-time Premier League winner Wayne Rooney.

The Manchester United's all-time top goal scorer confirmed the rumours with a hilarious tweet shortly after the surgery in 2011, stating that he was ‘going bald at 25’ and so thought ‘why not’.

This playful response to what at the time was a large amount of media pressure was a hilarious tactic which perhaps helped normalise and popularise the procedure.

Since then, Rooney has maintained his hair with further transplants and other procedures.

The former Champions League winner has possibly not just been to the surgeons’ office for his hair.

As when looking at the before and after photos of Rooney from a few years ago compared to him at the World Cup this summer, Harley Street surgeon Dr. Ivy suggested that, it is likely he has also indulged partially in some botox tweaks as well as a small number of dermal fillers.

However, Rooney has never mentioned any work like this being done before.

Wayne Rooney struggled with hair loss in his late teens and into his early twenties (left - pictured in 2010) and underwent the first of two hair transplants in 2011 (right - pictured in 2011)

Fans commented during the World Cup that the pundit had enjoyed a 'glow up'

Alejandro Garnacho

Another former Manchester United man to have visited the dentist is polarising winger, Alejandro Garnacho.

Garnacho's teeth were bared when he scored his first Premier League goal for Man United against Fulham in 2022.

Naturally earning comparisons to a young Ronaldo, Garnacho appeared to follow in his idol's footsteps by getting his own set of pristine porcelain veneers.

Unfortunately for the Argentine this is where the comparisons to Ronaldo abruptly end.

Alejandro Garnancho first burst onto the scene at Man United before moving to Chelsea

The winger followed in Ronaldo's path by getting a set of white veneers

Sergio Ramos

The next inclusion in this list may come as a surprise to some fans, as the tough tackling, card addict Sergio Ramos does not immediately strike one as a player who would indulge in cosmetic treatments.

Experts, however, believe the multiple Champions League winning captain has had a decent amount of work done.

It is considered extremely likely that the Spaniard has had work done on his teeth and lower face to provide a sharper smile as well as minimal botox alongside rhinoplasty work on his nose.

This has helped among other changes to transform the World Cup winner from a long haired, skinny, unassuming young lad into a tatted, sharp and imposing man.

Former Spain and Real Madrid star Sergio Ramos looks distinctly different to the start of his playing career

Ramos has reportedly undergone a series of cosmetic treatments over the years

Neymar

Neymar is also a member of the stellar list of players that have had some help from cosmetic surgeons. Like many of his Brazilian teammates the former Champions League winner has had a good amount of work done on his teeth, including a fresh set of veneers and dental bonding finished off with some light gum contouring.

Naturally Neymar enlisted the services of the best dental surgeons available and found great personal success, however the style of blinding bright veneers is still a brave one in places as the look still divides opinion amongst football fans and the public. Yet I don’t imagine the Brazilian himself will have any regrets.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola's first sit-down as Liverpool manager: New boss reveals his blueprint to restore Liverpool's identity with teamwork and faith in youth among his key principles
Sports.content:
They do things differently in the Basque Country, especially in Bilbao at Athletic Club. Not too differently, mind, to Liverpool.

An unwavering, indefatigable sense of identity. An us-against-them mentality, two fingers to the establishment. A philosophy that extends to football, with a belief in promoting youth and prioritising the collective over any one ego or individual.

It is for this reason that Liverpool and new head coach Andoni Iraola believe they have found the perfect marriage.

This feeling of worth is a topic that repeatedly surfaces during a lengthy chat with the man tasked with leading Liverpool back to glory, in his first sit-down interview since taking over from the sacked Arne Slot.

‘People ask me a lot why a lot of Basque managers especially have arrived to this level and why a lot of Spanish teams are winning a lot of things,’ says Iraola, in an Apprentice-style boardroom at a high-rise, swanky hotel in downtown Chicago.

‘I always say that a sense of collectiveness is very important. Spain has never had the best athletes. If you analyse, in swimming, track and field, they don't normally win medals.

Andoni Iraola is in his second month in charge of Liverpool as he looks to reinvigorate the Reds

The 44-year-old's football identity comes from his home in the Basque Country, Spain, where he spent over a decade at Athletic Bilbao as a player

‘But in collective sports they are very good. In football, basketball, handball, hockey.... normally they have good teams. We always put the team first.

‘An example is someone like Rodri. He didn't score or make an assist but at the end they won the World Cup and he won best player of the tournament. “Team first” was always integrated in how we're raised.’

It is pertinent because Spain were crowned world champions less than 48 hours before our chat. Through the tinted glass behind Iraola sits a group of well-to-do individuals sipping on Margaritas and Aperol Spritz, dining on small plates.

Iraola sticks to the black coffee for now. He was up at 4am due to jet-lag and perhaps a sense of nerves ahead of his first pre-season tour.

Spain also won the Euros. The Premier League winning manager? San Sebastian-born Mikel Arteta. Champions League? Gijon-born Luis Enrique, twice in a row. Both English domestic cups? Barcelona-born Pep Guardiola. Europa League? Unai Emery, another Basque.

Basque, Spanish, Catalan, they are the kings of football. And queens – the Spaniards are the reigning Women’s World Cup champions, too.

Liverpool and Chelsea have both appointed Basques in Iraola and his old mate Xabi Alonso, while Fulham have also gone for a Spaniard in Alvaro Arbeloa. It’s the biggest Spanish invasion since the conquistadors of the Aztec and Inca empires.

Iraola adds: ‘There has to be something in society. It cannot only just be about football. Things work when we are not just selfish, no? When, in the end, you prioritise the situation of the one who has less. That happens also in football.

‘The ones that don’t play, the ones who come from the academy, the ones who earn less. It could be a reference, you can compare it with society.

‘I see a lot of things (similar to Liverpool). This sense of belonging, of being a little bit different. This connection, also, with players from the academy. The atmosphere of Anfield.

‘This is one of the biggest clubs in the world and, in some way, the comparison to Athletic Club probably isn’t fair. But in a lot of ways I see a lot of things similar.’

There are now a number of Basque managers such as Mikel Arteta (left) and Xabi Alonso (right) in the Premier League

By the end of the Slot era, the Dutchman was criticised for pretty much everything. The fans had seen enough. The methods he was heralded as a genius for having 12 months earlier were now reasons for him to be sacked. It turned sour, nasty and toxic.

One stick to beat him with was how he did not immerse himself in the culture of the city. Iraola has already done that. A fan of the Christmas markets when he visited as a tourist several years ago, the former Bournemouth boss wants to experience all the cultural sites.

Iraola skipped going on holiday this summer – save for a brief trip back to Bilbao – to focus on finding a house and schools for his two kids. When asked what he enjoys doing in his spare time, Iraola gave a deadpan response: ‘I have two kids.’

So that’s that, then. Football and full-time fatherhood. He does make time, though, for his other great hobby: cycling. He unwinds by watching the Tour de France and is fascinated by the discipline – physical and mental – of top-level cyclists.

He loved the New Forest and other routes Dorset had to offer during his three seasons at Bournemouth, nearly as much as his homeland.

Iraola has already been given a few recommendations for bike rides in Merseyside and believes the helmet and wind-mask will help conceal his identity.

Another stick with which to beat Slot was his stubborn backing of struggling players and reluctance to promote youth (though he did play an integral part in the rise of 17-year-old sensation Rio Ngumoha).

Iraola, back on the topic of Bilbao, is a huge believer in promoting from within. At Athletic Club, the name anglicised as it was founded by British workers, he had no choice. Their famed La Cantera policy insists every player has to have Basque heritage.

‘It is a very special club,’ says Iraola, believing his roots there have served him well. ‘At Athletic Club, you have to maximise every player you have in the squad. You cannot sell him and choose another one a lot of times.

‘As a player, you have to give extra. The only way that policy can be successful is if you give 100 per cent. This creates a connection and you see they win things, they have never been relegated.’

Iraola's biggest inspiration is Athletic Bilbao and former Barcelona boss Ernesto Valverde

Iraola played 510 times for them, captaining them to a Europa League final under Marcelo Bielsa. He watched from afar in 2024 when players ditched a traditional bus parade to sail down the Nervion, banks filled by millions, on a barge with the Copa del Rey, a first trophy since 1984.

The manager of that triumph was the man who left the biggest impression on Iraola: Ernesto Valverde. The two-time La Liga winner with Barcelona, who managed Athletic three times, was on Liverpool’s list to replace Jurgen Klopp due to his playing style.

‘I had very good managers as a player,’ explains Iraola when asked about his coaching idols. ‘If I have to choose one, I always say Ernesto Valverde.

‘I had him when I was in the academy and he was the one who gave me the chance to play in the first team. I also had him towards the end of my Athletic Club career. I learned a lot from him. Everyone asks me about Marcelo Bielsa.

‘I also had some games with the national team with Vicente del Bosque (World Cup winner in 2010 and Euros in 2012).

‘They were good managers. Even at the end of my career, playing for Patrick Vieira after I signed for New York City, gave me a different perspective. But if I have to pick one, then it's Valverde.

‘It was his common sense. He never made problems bigger than they were. He always understood the players. He was very firm with the things he believed in. But how he treated the players, both those who were playing and those who weren't, I liked it a lot.’

Iraola knows he has a sizeable task on his hands, especially after the cloud of negativity that lingered over last season where Champions League qualification was only achieved on the final weekend.

Slot’s football was tough to watch at times, though the players were not exempt from blame. The famous Anfield atmosphere subsequently became non-existent and the ground stopped being a fortress.

The new man is keen to put all that right.

‘The first thing is try to play well,’ he says. ‘Football is what helps you more, but it’s not just only about playing well. This helps a lot but I think the supporters have to feel identified with what they see on the pitch.

The new Liverpool boss is looking to bring back the connection between the fans and the squad that was lost last season

‘Sometimes it's not about just putting one ball in the top corner. A lot of times the ones watching the game are… OK, they cannot do it, but they can run, they can fight for the balls, they can press, they can fight until the last minute for every situation.

‘When they see this from the players of their team it’s easier to get behind that team. I will encourage my team to give them these things.

‘The most important thing that we can deliver is our performances. It doesn't matter if I speak well, if I don't speak well, if I say the right things or if I don’t say the right things. At the end people just want to see the team play well and deliver good results.

‘I know this is 90 per cent of my job.

‘For me, now, it is about creating a very good team, a very difficult team to beat. The team that I envision now, that I see and think of, if we become that team, I think we are going to be successful.’

Iraola’s team are at a training camp in Chicago ahead of a three-leg tour of America. The squad fly to Nashville on Friday to take on Sunderland there, before games against Wrexham in New York City and Leeds back here in the so-called Windy City.

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola set to REJECT Italy after 'demanding huge £17m-a-year salary' - as the Azzurri struggle to fund move despite vowing to make 'financial exceptions' for former Man City boss
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola set to REJECT Italy after 'demanding huge £17m-a-year salary' - as the Azzurri struggle to fund move despite vowing to make 'financial exceptions' for former Man City boss

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Pep Guardiola is reportedly set to reject Italy despite 'financial exceptions' having been made in an attempt to attract the legendary Manchester City boss.

Guardiola is currently out of work after leaving City at the end of last season following 10 incredible years in England where he won 20 trophies.

The Italian Football Federation (FIGC), meanwhile, have been searching for a new manager since Gennaro Gattuso resigned in April after the Azzurri failed to qualify for a third successive World Cup.

FIGC chief Giovanni Malago had outlined their interest in Guardiola earlier this week along with his determination to get a deal done at a time where the country's football team are experiencing some of their worst ever times on the football pitch.

But, according to Italian outlet Gazzetta dello Sport, the Spaniard is unlikely to take the role despite meeting with the FIGC's technical director Paolo Maldini and his adviser Leonardo in Barcelona last weekend.

The report states that although Malago highlighted how his federation were willing to break the bank for No 1 target Guardiola, the two parties remain far apart on figures.

Pep Guardiola is reportedly set to reject the opportunity to take over as Italy's new manager

Italy have failed to qualify for the last three World Cups and currently do not have a manager

It is understood that Guardiola wants a salary of €20million-a-year (£17m), but the FIGC have only offered around €10m-a-year (£8.5m).

The report adds that although Maldini and Leonardo, who previously served as PSG's sporting director, have a superb relationship with Guardiola, they returned from their meeting in Barcelona with 'little optimism'.

This was despite Guardiola - who spent two seasons in Italy during his playing days with Brescia and Roma and can speak the language - being offered a comprehensive project where he would have significant control over Italian football.

The 55-year-old is understood to be concerned about the commitment required by jumping straight back into management having promised his family that he would live in Barcelona now his time in England has come to an end.

Unless they give their blessing to the Italy role, it seems unlikely that Guardiola will accept the offer.

Speaking earlier this week about the former Man City, Barcelona and Bayern Munich boss, Malago had said: '[Financial] exceptions have been made, exceptions that for example may concern the name that is so overbearing in these hours: Pep Guardiola.

'Exceptions for obvious reasons that I am not here to explain, but it is not certain that this thing will go through.'

Former Italy boss Roberto Mancini and Azzurri legend Andrea Pirlo are also in the running for the role, although the likes of Antonio Conte may come into the mix if Guardiola does reject the opportunity.

Italy Under 21 boss Silvio Baldini was in temporary charge for the June international break, yet with a fresh cycle starting after the World Cup, they are keen to appoint a new manager as soon as possible.

Sports.title: How Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes proved in just 45 minutes that this is a whole new Tottenham this season - and why £185m duo's new team-mates could barely believe their eyes
Sports.content:
If first impressions are anything to go by, then Tottenham Hotspur should get used to controlling midfield.

Their new-look £185million pivot dictated play in their opening pre-season friendly – a 1-0 win against MK Dons on Wednesday – providing a 45-minute glimpse of what to expect from club record-breaking transfers Sandro Tonali (£100m from Newcastle) and Mateus Fernandes (£85m from West Ham).

Let’s get the balancing act out of the way. Yes, it was only a pre-season match. Yes, it was only one half of football. And yes, it was against inferior League One opposition, MK Dons.

But their desire to impose themselves immediately was encouraging. Fernandes took just three minutes to exhibit his natural ability. MK Dons goalkeeper Craig MacGillivray punched Mathys Tel’s corner clear, but Fernandes lurked outside the area and wrapped his right foot around the ball on the volley and hammered it into the top corner.

Pre-season or not, it was a top-quality finish - a sneak peek at his talent. Seeing the first manifestation of his £85m transfer fee, his new team-mates laughed in disbelief when the ball hit the back of the net. Spurs chiefs would have celebrated with a sigh of relief as he demonstrated the first sign of being a hit.

What a hit, Mateus Fernandes 💥



Watch our pre-season games live on SPURSPLAY! — Tottenham Hotspur (@SpursOfficial) July 22, 2026

Mateus Fernandes finds the top corner inside five minutes of his Tottenham debut

Sandro Tonali, whose fee could rise to £100million, also impressed in the pre-season friendly

Spurs changed their entire XI at half-time – as is customary at the start of pre-season – making the sample size small. Regardless, it was an extremely active debut. Everything went through Fernandes – he had 81 touches in the first half; no player had more.

Playing as a No 8, he was supported by fellow new arrival Tonali in a more deep-lying role. And for a pair playing together for the first time, they showed a surprising level of synchronisation. They both picked up on each other’s movement, finding space or covering when the other was on the ball.

If that can be developed in a week, then Spurs are on the right footing with this pair as they attempt to return to the top half after finishing 17th in consecutive seasons – avoiding relegation last term by just two points. Much like Fernandes, Tonali was busy – registering 70 touches; only his midfield partner had more.

Tonali was given the licence to run forward into the channels from his holding midfield role as Spurs tried to break down MK Dons’ disciplined, low block. The Italian is versatile; not only is he a ball-winner, but he has a big engine and an array of line-breaking passes at his disposal. It enables him to play as a six or an eight. Partnering Fernandes, however, it seems that can be relatively fluid.

Perhaps the biggest boost is that Spurs’ lavish midfield is well-rested after Italy failed to qualify for the World Cup, while Portugal overlooked Fernandes. It offers Roberto De Zerbi a full pre-season to get his ideas across to the heartbeat of the team, the anchors between defence and attack – a luxury that most managers do not have this summer.

What remains to be seen, though, is how they will handle teams that pose a greater threat. There was little forthcoming from the MK Dons attack, and they did not have much of the ball, which limited the occasions Spurs could press with intensity – a hallmark of De Zerbi’s teams.

The pair will need to step up to the increased workload, and that process should begin to take shape as the quality of opposition increases.

Tottenham will now jet Down Under, facing Auckland FC, Sydney FC and Chelsea, before returning to north London to play Getafe and Hoffenheim, with little under a month to go until the Premier League opener at Brentford on August 22.

Fernandes and Tonali are among £240m worth of reinforcements given to Roberto De Zerbi this summer

There were a couple of mistakes. Both gave the ball away in dangerous areas as MK Dons embarked on encouraging counter-attacks. Tonali was bailed out by an offside flag, Fernandes by a lung-busting run from a recovering defender. The pair deserve the benefit of the doubt for a couple of misplaced passes at the start of pre-season, though.

It was an exhibition of intelligent passes in the main – particularly from Tonali, who played a pivotal role in transition as he shifted the ball into wide areas.

His highlight came as he carried the ball from deep towards the halfway line before disguising a bending pass with his right foot into the feet of Tel, who cut inside and squared to Conor Gallagher inside the penalty area. An incisive move from back to front – crafted by Tonali – Gallagher couldn’t quite connect to top it off.

On the basis of this showing, the Englishman will need to step it up to keep up with Spurs' new dynamic duo.

Sports.title: F1 news: Kimi Antonelli replaced at Hungarian Grand Prix as Red Bull enquiries emerge
Sports.content:
F1 news: Kimi Antonelli replaced at Hungarian Grand Prix as Red Bull enquiries emerge

A look at the latest F1 headlines ahead of the Hungarian Grand Prix

View 3 Images Kimi Antonelli boasts a big lead at the top of the drivers' standings (Image: Getty Images)

The F1 circus is gearing up for its final race weekend before the summer shutdown, with Kimi Antonelli looking to extend his lead in the drivers' standings. Having seen his advantage eroded by the poor reliability of his Mercedes, the teenage sensation was imperious in Belgium last weekend, winning the race at a canter from Ferrari's Charles Leclerc.

‌



Meanwhile, Mercedes team-mate George Russell had a shocker, qualifying fourth and then crashing out on the first lap after making contact with Lewis Hamilton's Ferrari. That left him 50 points behind Antonelli and five points off Hamilton.

‌



Russell desperately needs a strong weekend at the tight and twisty Hungaroring near Budapest. At a circuit where engine performance is as critical as at Spa, Ferrari and Red Bull will hope to be in the fight for race victory.

‌



Another weekend of Antonelli dominance would deal a hammer blow to his rivals, especially Russell. Ahead of the Hungarian Grand Prix, here's a round-up of the latest F1 news…

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Red Bull inundated

Red Bull have been inundated by drivers interested in joining the team amid uncertainty over Max Verstappen's future. The four-time world champion, who has been linked with Mercedes and McLaren, holds the key to the driver market.

‌



Lewis Hamilton punishment confirmed after Belgian GP incident left F1 star with broken leg fear READ MORE :

A clause in his contract would allow him to quit the team at the end of this season. Despite his continuing frustration with the pace of the Red Bull and the sport's current regulations, he looks more likely to change teams for 2028, as it stands.

With Verstappen considering his options, Red Bull need to prepare for life without F1's best driver. And according to team principal Laurent Mekies, several drivers have been in touch about the potential vacancy.

Mekies told Sky Sports F1: "Look, it is working in both directions. It is completely natural that Max gets a call from everyone, because he is the best driver in the world.

‌



View 3 Images Laurent Mekies is waiting for Max Verstappen to decide on his future (Image: Getty Images)

"And equally, if you are a top team, you are going to get calls from many of these good drivers around as well. So that's natural. Is it a distraction for us? Not really.

"Our full focus is on getting that car as fast as it can [be] and then you will keep your best driver in the world. And we also see the massive growth of Isack [Hadjar] alongside Max, and that for us is the ideal pairing and we try to make sure we can keep that pairing."

‌



Antonelli replaced

The championship leader is among several top drivers who will be replaced for the first practice session in Hungary. F1 teams are mandated to run rookies in at least two sessions in both cars over the course of a season.

Antonelli will hand his car over to Mercedes reserve driver Frederik Vesti. The Dane has already had a stint in Antonelli's car this season after getting a runout in FP1 at the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix.

View 3 Images Antonelli will sit out part of the Hungarian Grand Prix weekend (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

Therefore, the Italian will not be obliged to give up his car for any further sessions this season. In contrast, Russell has not been replaced for any practice sessions yet, meaning he will have to hand his car over on two occasions once the season resumes after the summer break.

McLaren's Oscar Piastri will also sit out the first practice session in Hungary, with Leonardo Fornaroli getting a runout. Meanwhile, Paul Aron (Alpine), Ryo Hirakawa (Haas) and Colton Herta (Cadillac) will replace Franco Colapinto, Oliver Bearman and Valtteri Bottas, respectively, in FP1.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury outweighed for first time in 15 years by 21-stone rival
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury outweighed for first time in 15 years by 21-stone rival

The 'Gypsy King' is rarely used to weighing less than his opponent, but Mariusz Wach towered over the British star ahead of their fight on Friday night

View Image Tyson Fury and Mariusz Wach weigh in ahead of their fight

Tyson Fury has been outweighed for the first time in well over a decade after being dwarfed by Mariusz Wach ahead of their fight.

‌



The two heavyweight scrappers will meet behind closed doors over in Thailand on Friday night. Very few will be able to attend tomorrow night's action - as Fury looks to get some crucial rounds under his belt before a monumental showdown with Anthony Joshua later this year.

‌



Fury ended a year-long hiatus back in April, outpointing Arslanbek Makhmudov in front of over 60,000 fans at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Watching ringside was long-time rival Joshua. While the Morecambe brawler demanded a face-off after the fight, 'AJ' refused. That said, the pair signed to fight just days later - which is expected to land in November, providing Joshua also wins his warm-up fight against Kristian Prenga.

‌



Despite being raring to go, Fury had the small task of making weight. Up first, was the 46-year-old Polish veteran - who weighed in a staggering 291.4lb. A rather stunned Fury was next, who tipped the scales at 265lb - 2lb lighter than he was when he faced Makhmudov earlier this year.

A rather lean Fury was shocked by the huge disparity in weight between the pair. Very few men know exactly what it feels like to come in heavier than the 'Gypsy King'. The last time this happened was back in 2011 when Derek Chisora came in just over 5lb more than Fury for their first encounter. John McDermott and Daniil Peretyatko are the only other two to have come in heavier than the British boxing icon.

Both Fury and Wach then came nose-to-nose one last time, with the former trying to get under his rival's skin and tower over the Polish fighter. There's clearly no animosity between the two as they both shared a rather warm embrace before eventually leaving the stage.

Speaking after weighing in, the 37-year-old said: "I've put in lots of work. I feel fitter, sharper and stronger. I've never faced a man heavier than me [sic]. I'm normally always the fat c***. I'm Mr Slim now. I'm delighted to be here and there is fans here from everyone all over the world.

Many assumed Fury would hop on a private jet after coming away unscathed against Wach to be ringside for Joshua's comeback fight over in Saudi Arabia - but that won't be the case. Sports.title: Madeleine McCann's brother Sean reveals 'excitement' before competing in Commonwealth Games
Sports.content:
Madeleine McCann's brother Sean reveals 'excitement' before competing in Commonwealth Games

Sean McCann, 21, who will make his first appearance at the Commonwealth Games, was just two years old when his sister Madeleine, three, disappeared from the family's holiday apartment in Portugal in 2007

Sean McCann is ready for home Commonwealth Games 2026

Madeleine McCann's younger brother has spoken of his excitement as he prepares to represent Scotland at the Commonwealth Games. Sean McCann, 21, is due to make his first appearance at Glasgow 2026 in the pool this weekend. Madeleine disappeared from her family's holiday apartment in Praia da Luz, Portugal, at the age of three, back in 2007, and has been missing ever since. Sean was just two years old at the time.

‌



McCann is a distance freestyler and is expected to compete in the freestyle relay events at the slimmed-down Games. Madeleine vanished on May 3, 2007 and has been missing since, presumed dead. Her disappearance prompted a worldwide manhunt.

‌



View 3 Images Sean McCann is swimming for Scotland (Image: Getty Images for Commonwealth Sport)

‌



Retirement warning for millions of people relying on money from family inheritance READ MORE :

Sean has enjoyed a meteoric rise in sport in recent years and is now looking ahead to the summer. He said: “I’m very excited, it’s my first senior games so I’m just looking forward to representing Scotland and doing my absolute best,” he said in a message released by Loughborough University, where he is a student. “It’s the pinnacle really of representing Scotland at the Commonwealth Games, especially at a home Games. I’ve got lots of family up in Glasgow so that makes it even more special.

"I was there in 2014 Commonwealth Games, watching as a kid, so to make it now, twelve years later, is really a full circle moment.” He said his studies and life at Loughborough helped him flourish. “At my home club I didn’t really have anyone doing the same events as me, which meant in training you were always working by yourself," he added.

View 3 Images Kate and Gerry McCann attend a press conference for the launch of the book 'Madeleine' in 2011 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



“But here, there’s always been people who are better than me, similar to me, so we push each other all the time. We’re all striving towards the same sort of things. You can never really slack off with the quality of athletes around you.

“You’ve got to have a strong mentality in distance swimming; I always tend to build my way into a race – that’s how I like to pace it. I’m going in as more of an underdog; I don’t feel like there’s any pressure on me. I should be able to go in and perform at my best.” McCann also spoke about what drew him to Loughborough as he balances sporting and educational priorities. “I study Chemical Engineering; I spoke to coaches in Britain, and they said ‘if you want to pursue distance swimming, this is where to go’," he added.

View 3 Images Sean McCann competing at a previous Youth Games event (Image: Facebook)

Article continues below

“Alongside that, it was number one for the degree as well, which made it the obvious choice in the end. There’s so much talent just around the campus. Wherever you go, you always see athletes around. The pool’s amazing, the gym’s amazing – it’s the place to be, and I really love training here.”

King Charles is expected to tell the audience about the importance of togetherness in his speech to open the Games tonight. KT Tunstall is headlining the show which takes place from 8pm to 10pm at Glasgow’s OVO Hydro. The 14,300-seater venue is more accustomed to hosting the world’s biggest music stars than international sporting events. Organisers describe the show as “a creative kaleidoscope and Clyde-built journey packed full of music, humour and Scottish surprise”. The King will formally declare the Games open by reading aloud the message he placed inside the King’s Baton at Buckingham Palace on Commonwealth Day, March 10 last year. It has spent the past 500 days travelling to all 74 competing nations and territories, each of which decorated its own version, before being reunited on stage during the Parade of Nations at the opening ceremony.

Sports.title: National Racehorse Week coming to Liverpool and Portsmouth with 76 yards open to public
Sports.content:
National Racehorse Week coming to Liverpool and Portsmouth with 76 yards open to public

Ollie Murphy, Joe Tizzard, Rebecca Menzies and Tim Vaughan will open their stables for the ten day nationwide event from August 22 to 31

View 2 Images Sam Quek and Chris Hughes in Chester during National Racehorse Week (Image: PA)

National Racehorse Week is set to return for the sixth year running and bookings are now open for this year’s ten-day programme.

‌



The nationwide event that will take place from August 22-31 will see a variety of training yards, studs and aftercare centres opening their doors to the public.

‌



This year 96 different racing venues across England, Scotland and Wales will be open to the public, alongside over 50 community events and three city activations held at some of England’s biggest cities and landmarks.

‌



Following the success of the racing pop-up in Chester city centre last year, three racing-themed pop-up experiences will arrive in city centres during the week, two in Liverpool and one in Portsmouth, when families who may never have visited a racecourse before have the chance to meet a racehorse.

Frankie Dettori responds to cheeky suggestion he could make another dramatic comeback READ MORE :

Spaces are available for more than 15,500 people to attend events this year, an increase on last year's figure of 14,800 free spaces available to book. During the event there will be 111 public open days across 96 venues including 76 training yards, 11 studs and nine aftercare centres

‌



Ollie Murphy, Joe Tizzard, Rebecca Menzies and Tim Vaughan are among the trainers who will host tours of their facilities, providing the chance to see horses exercise on the gallops, and on the treadmills and walkers.

Murphy who is based in Warwickshire and is opening his doors to 2,000 guests this year, said: “National Racehorse week is a brilliant initiative that I am proud to have been a part of across the last four years.

View 2 Images Over 90 stables, studs and aftercare centres will be open to the public (Image: Cotswold Film/Louis Gill)

Article continues below

“It is an incredibly important event for our sport, and it is great to welcome newcomers, curious minds and sport lovers to learn more year in year out. With 2025 seeing around 700 people visiting us at Warren Chase, I hope to see even more faces joining us this year.”

Since its inception National Racehorse Week has delivered 65,000 free places for the public to visit studs, training yards, and retraining centres for free and put on an additional 190 community events connecting over 10,000 additional people.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua makes offer to Tyson Fury ahead of mega-fight
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua makes offer to Tyson Fury ahead of mega-fight

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury are finally expected to trade leather this year, and the latter has reignited their feud by throwing a verbal jab at his long-time rival

View Image Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua

Anthony Joshua has offered to help train Tyson Fury to lose weight ahead of their all-British clash later this year.

The 36-year-old will make a return to the ring on Saturday night in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, against Kristian Prenga. 'AJ' has not fought since knocking out boxing novice Jake Paul in the sixth round back in December. He had been expected to fight in March, but was involved in a tragic car crash just days after his win over the 'Problem Child.;

However, seven months on, the Brit will make his highly-anticipated return to the ring. A day before his fight with the Albanian, though, rival Fury is also in action. The 'Gypsy King' will take on Mariusz Wach over in Thailand. While the Morecambe brawler has repeatedly played down talks of a fight with Joshua, he still cannot seem to get his rival out of his mind.

Over the years, Fury has tried to spark a verbal war with Joshua, but the latter has risen above it. That said, after being branded a 'bodybuilder' for the millionth time, the Watford native just had to bite back.

Providing both men come away from their respective warm-up fights unscathed, they will finally meet in the ring. The pair have been on a collision course for over a decade, but are still yet to settle their difference. The all-British dust-up is expected to take place in November - with the UK the frontrunner to host - or so we thought.

However, recent reports have emerged that the contest could now take place in New York as talks continue over a venue. Saudi boxing supremo Turki Alalshikh is insisting on a late start time in the UK in order to capture the American TV market. This means the clash could be moved over to the US - with promoter Eddie Hearn revealing it could land at Madison Square Garden in New York. But a lot of the Americans want to do it at MSG; not Vegas, they want it at MSG."

Sports.title: Frankie Dettori responds to cheeky suggestion he could make another dramatic comeback
Sports.content:
Frankie Dettori responds to cheeky suggestion he could make another dramatic comeback

The Italian rode competitively for last time in Brazil in February but has now been linked with a return with Amo Racing, for whom he is an ambassador

View Image Jockey Frankie Dettori celebrates with owner Kia Joorabchian after winning the Qipco Champion Stakes

Frankie Dettori has responded to a cheeky suggestion he could make another dramatic comeback.

‌



The Italian rode for the final time in Brazil in February after taking his farewell tour to South America. The legendary jockey had originally scheduled his retirement for Champions Day at Ascot in October 2023 only to reverse his decision to call it a day and continue his career in the US.

‌



The 55-year-old confirmed last November that his time there would come to an end at the Breeders’ Cup at Del Mar ahead of a short farewell trip to South America which ended in Rio de Janeiro.

‌



Aidan O'Brien compares Benvenuto Cellini to Galileo ahead of King George at Ascot READ MORE :

He has since taken on a role as ambassador for Kia Joorabchian’s Amo Racing, representing the football agent on the racecourse.

But rumours have surfaced about the future of the team’s retained jockey David Egan after he was overlooked for some of the Amo rides.

Joorabchian has made no comment while Egan addressed the speculation after riding a winner at Leicester on Wednesday night.

‌



“There’s been no quotes from anyone and I’d like to say no comment from me,” he told RacingTV.

“I’ve got no comment on the situation. I’m declared to ride a horse on Friday for Amo, plan to ride for him on Saturday and even into next week so no comment.”

Nevertheless online bookmaker Betway fed the rumour mill by speculating whether Dettori could be in line for a dramatic comeback.

‌



The firm offered odds of 4-1 that he would ride for Amo Racing in the UK before the end of 2027.

Spokesperson Lewis Knowles said: ''Frankie has certainly been the comeback king over the years, with more than one retirement U-turn, so you could never truly rule out a return to the saddle at some stage.

“His relationship with Kia Joorabchian and the Amo Racing operation as Racing Manager is seemingly going from strength to strength, and with a retained rider vacancy very much open, it's certainly not beyond the realms of possibility that we could see the great man in those famous purple silks once again.''

Article continues below

Dettori responded with a laughing emoji.

Sports.title: FIFA announce World Cup team of the tournament as baffled fans say 'what a joke'
Sports.content:
FIFA announce World Cup team of the tournament as baffled fans say 'what a joke'

The World Cup team of the tournament that FIFA revealed has left fans baffled because there are some players who can count themselves unfortunate not to feature

View 2 Images Fans online are fuming about the lack of Spain players in FIFA's Dream XI (Image: Getty Images)

FIFA's fan-voted World Cup dream XI does not feature Golden Glove winner Unai Simon or Young Player Award recipient Pau Cubarsi. Vozinha is in goal with almost 40% of the votes, while Dayot Upemecano and Lisandro Martinez are the two central defenders chosen by fans.

‌



Of those two, the France international received the most votes, with nearly 15%, while his defensive partner in this team barely managed 10%. The two full-backs selected are Marc Cucurella and Pedro Porro, both of Spain.

‌



Real Madrid's new left-back won 23% of the vote. His international team-mate is on the right with approaching 19%.

‌



Lots of fans online have been left happy that Spain's goalkeeper and teenage defender are not included, though. In response to a FIFA social media post announcing the team, many expressed their feelings.

A further user replied on X: "This should be a prank, right? Where's Cubarsi? Where's Simon, who collected the Golden Glove?" One more asked: "Martinez over Cubarsi? Are we for real… him, Laporte and Unai kept it only one goal all World Cup."

There were, though, fewer complaints about the rest of the team. England star Jude Bellingham, Michael Olise and Rodri make up the midfield three.

However, despite receiving the Golden Ball, Spain's captain has just 15% of the vote. That total is some way behind Bronze Boot winner Bellingham's 29% and Olise's 19%.

‌



Erling Haaland, Kylian Mbappe and Lionel Messi are the front three. This summer's Golden Boot and Bronze Ball winner leads the way with almost 30% of the vote, with Haaland on 27% and Messi at 22%, despite having a Silver Ball and Silver Boot to go along with his runners-up medal.

The vote was open for 48 hours after the World Cup final. There were also votes for the standout players - one goalkeeper, one defender, one midfielder and one forward - after every round throughout the tournament to build a shortlist.

The four winners from each round made the shortlist. They joined "additional players identified by FIFA based on their performances during the tournament". Cubarsi was not the top-voted defender after any of the seven rounds.

Simon did make it with almost 45% of the goalkeeper vote after the semi-finals. Vozinha, however, averaged 50% when winning round one and the round of 32.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
